title: Héctor "Pochola" Silva into World Rugby Hall of Fame
article_text:
World Rugby announced that it will welcome seven players into its Hall of Fame over the coming months. One of them is from the Americas. It is former Puma and Pumas coach, Héctor “Pochola” Silva. Rugby was in his blood with his contribution to Argentine rugby also running deep at Los Tilos club.

Silva will be posthumously inducted in Buenos Aires on December 14 during the UAR annual dinner. He will become the seventh Argentine player inducted into the World Rugby Hall of Fame.

Pochola started playing rugby aged 14. At age 20, he earned his call-up to Los Pumas for the 1965 tour of South Africa. He was a Puma from 1965-1980 and earned 25 test caps.

On September 23, 2017, an emotional ceremony was held at the Los Tilos grounds, where the club’s main field, Pitch No. 1, was officially named “Héctor Pochola Silva.” Silva attended the tribute and expressed his gratitude for receiving such an honor during his lifetime. He passed away in May 2021 from COVID-19.

title: England star could miss Six Nations after latest injury setback
article_text:
Alex Mitchell is facing a lengthy spell on the sidelines after undergoing surgery on his latest hamstring injury, with the England scrum-half potentially set to miss the 2027 Six Nations.

The 29-year-old has been struggling with recurring hamstring problems throughout 2026 and is now facing an extended period of rehabilitation after going under the knife.

Mitchell picked up his latest injury while playing for Northampton Saints in their Gallagher PREM victory over Gloucester at Franklin’s Gardens on October 31.

He was forced off after just 21 minutes, with Jonny Weimann coming on as his replacement. The injury subsequently ruled him out of England’s Nations Championship squad for their November fixtures.

The Northampton scrum-half has since travelled to Finland to undergo surgery with Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in elite sporting injuries.

It is the fourth hamstring injury Mitchell has suffered this year.

He previously damaged the same hamstring against Ireland in February and Fiji in July, while also picking up an issue with his left hamstring during an England training camp in May.

Mitchell, who was Steve Borthwick's first-choice scrum-half last season, has managed to return ahead of schedule from previous injuries.

However, an estimated four-month rehabilitation would leave him with little time to force his way back into contention for the Six Nations.

England's campaign begins before Mitchell would be expected to return, although there is a possibility he could feature in the final two rounds against Wales and Scotland on March 6 and 13 respectively.

Borthwick now has three main options at scrum-half, with Jack van Poortvliet, Ben Spencer and Mitchell's Northampton teammate Archie McParland all available.

Van Poortvliet currently appears to be the leading candidate for the starting shirt, having been entrusted with the role during Mitchell's absence.

Tommy Freeman was a late withdrawal from England's victory over New Zealand yesterday after picking up a thigh niggle.

The winger was replaced in the starting XV by Cadan Murley around an hour before kick-off.

His availability for next week's Nations Championship finals weekend rematch against the All Blacks remains unclear.

title: Hollie Davidson named 'best referee' after decision left Argentina star fuming
article_text:
Hollie Davidson has been hailed as the "best referee in world rugby" after her impressive performance in France's clash with Argentina, which included a contentious decision that left Pumas captain Julian Montoya furious.

The Scottish official earned widespread praise for her handling of the contest in Paris, with former England captain Will Carling among those to single her out for special recognition.

One incident in particular caught the attention of viewers, with Davidson standing firm after Montoya angrily protested a decision at the breakdown.

With France leading 26-10, a penalty was awarded against the Argentina skipper following a chaotic passage of play at a ruck.

France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey had initially flown into the breakdown, before Montoya then attempted to steal possession, only for Davidson to penalise him for going off his feet.

The Argentina captain was incensed by the decision, repeatedly shouting "It's the same!" as he pointed out what he believed was a similar infringement by Bielle-Biarrey moments earlier.

Davidson was unmoved, telling Montoya: "Off feet, you're driving over the breakdown."

The exchange came during a difficult spell for Argentina, with Montoya subsequently sent to the sin bin.

Former France hooker Benjamin Kayser, working as co-commentator, was full of praise for Davidson's handling of the situation.

"Hollie Davidson, having absolutely none of it!" he exclaimed.

"Julian Montoya was fuming at this decision. But I think she is absolutely spot on.

"The clearout from Louis Bielle-Biarrey, then [Montoya] goes around and he dives on it."

Davidson's performance throughout the contest attracted considerable attention on social media, with many supporters praising her authority, communication and consistency.

Former England captain Carling was particularly impressed, suggesting she had outperformed every other official involved in the weekend's international fixtures.

Writing on X, he said: "One other observation about all the great games yesterday - how good was Hollie Davidson - I thought she was easily the best referee - eagle eyed, calm, authoritative when needed, sympathetic when needed - and used the TMO quickly and precisely - loved it."

His assessment prompted a wave of agreement from rugby supporters, who were similarly impressed by the Scottish referee's display.

One fan responded: "She was absolutely tip top."

Another wrote: "Absolutely. She is getting the big games based on merit alone. That's all the game wants - the best refs. She is one them."

A third simply declared: "She's fantastic!"

Others suggested Davidson's rise through the refereeing ranks was an encouraging sign for rugby more generally.

"Apart from her own achievements, it reflects really well on the progress the game has made," one supporter wrote.

Another added: "She is a brilliant ref."

One fan praised her no-nonsense approach, writing: "Well said. She's a top ref, takes no nonsense."

Davidson, 34, has established herself as one of the most highly regarded officials in international rugby, earning increasingly prominent appointments in the men's game.

Her latest performance only strengthened that reputation, with another supporter writing: "100% agree - at only 34yo Hollie Davidson is a great example for those who wish to officiate at all levels in the game that we have grown to know and love."

title: Andy Farrell praises Sam Prendergast’s response after South Africa criticism
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Andy Farrell believes Sam Prendergast emerged from a pre-match storm fuelled by South Africa’s coaching staff to show exactly what he is capable of.

Fly-half Prendergast ultimately landed the decisive penalty in Saturday’s statement 20-17 win over the world champions in Dublin after avoiding retrospective punishment for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji.

Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus branded Prendergast’s challenge “terrible” but predicted he would be cleared to play on a “technicality” during a controversial press conference on Monday.

Erasmus’ assistant Mzwandile Stick continued the criticism on Friday, saying: “If that was a Fijian player, he would be sitting in Fiji now doing some extra lessons of how to tackle.”

Ireland head coach Farrell made clear his unhappiness with the inflammatory comments from the opposition camp as he praised Prendergast’s response.

“I didn’t like all that,” he said. “It carried on during the week as well, didn’t it? I didn’t like all that about Sam because Sam was cleared, and I was there while he was cleared.

“Sam’s done nothing wrong and I was so proud of him in the sense that he played like that.

“Nothing bothered him, I thought he was excellent. He had the courage to play the balls out the back, play quickly, and play to space. I thought it was an excellent game from him all round.”

After Robert Baloucoune scored two first-half tries and Ronan Kelleher added another, Prendergast nervelessly split the posts from distance in the 54th minute before a heroic defensive display secured victory.

Prendergast, 23, also received a glowing endorsement from half-back partner Jamison Gibson-Park.

“He’s come on leaps and bounds I think in the last little while,” said the scrum-half.

“He’s just taken it all in his stride and the most impressive thing is he’s just able to bounce into the next moment and I know that’s something he’s working hard on but I’m pretty proud of the guy.

“He’s been through a lot and he’s playing some good footy so I’m very happy for him.”

Ireland laid down a marker ahead of next year’s World Cup with an overdue – and thoroughly deserved – success over one of rugby’s top-ranked nations.

Their scrum was comprehensively outmuscled by South Africa in a 24-13 Dublin defeat last November, while they have lost their last four meetings with New Zealand and last two with France.

Farrell has now won four of six encounters with the Springboks after celebrating another memorable victory of his reign, secured in front of a capacity Aviva Stadium crowd.

“It’s another massive game so it has to be up there (as one of the best),” he said.

“It’s what we also expect of ourselves – not to beat South Africa but to keep growing and delivering, certainly at home. It certainly matters a lot to us.”

Captain Dan Sheehan, who started at number eight for the first time at Test level, relished the challenge of taking on a different role having won his previous 42 caps at hooker.

He said: “It wasn’t perfect by any means but something different keeps your mind busy and almost gives me a distraction from thinking about the game too much.

“I was pretty happy with how the lads fronted up, especially in the pack. I thought we kept our calm pretty well at times and backed ourselves when it mattered.

“We talked about it all week, about making sure we front up on big days like this and the privilege of having the world champions in our back garden and for lads to show up meant a lot.”

Ireland will play Australia in the Nations Championship fifth-place final at Twickenham on Friday evening.

title: Wales star Tomos Williams stood down with immediate effect
article_text:
Steve Tandy has provided an injury update on Tomos Williams after the Wales scrum-half has emerged as a doubt for next weekend’s clash against Japan.

Williams suffered a groin problem during Wales’ dramatic 29-26 defeat against Australia at Principality Stadium.

Wales head coach Tandy confirmed that the Saracens player's injury will be assessed over the coming days.

His absence would be another concern after the Wallabies brought them back down to earth just seven days after ending their 73-year wait for a victory over the All Blacks.

Speaking after the match, a subdued Tandy offered a relatively positive initial assessment but also mentioned the possibility of replacing Williams for the encounter against Japan.

“Tomos is just a bit tight in his groin,” admitted Tandy.

“We will assess that as we go, but we have got options.

“I thought Reuben (Morgan-Williams) did really well when he came on.”

Wales now face a nervous wait over Williams’ availability as their attention is firmly fixed on the Brave Blossoms at Allianz Stadium.

Potentially, Tandy may have to reshuffle, which could see Reuben Morgan-Williams or uncapped Che Hope in line if the experienced scrum-half fails to recover.

Captain Dewi Lake scored twice, with Blair Murray and Ryan Elias also crossing, but those four crosses were not enough to prevent Wales from suffering a narrow three-point defeat.

Tandy confirmed that changes are likely for Wales’ final Nations Championship match as he looks to freshen up his side following a demanding campaign.

“We will definitely look at that,” continued Tandy.

“The boys have got a couple days off now.

“We will look at the changing room and see where we are with injuries.

“We will definitely freshen things up for next week.”

Tandy will select his Wales side to face Japan on Thursday.

title: Wales to make changes for Nations Championship finale as fringe stars to get chance
article_text:
Steve Tandy has vowed to rotate his side for their final Nations Championship match against Japan in London next week.

Wales will take on the Brave Blossoms for the fifth time in 16 months, as the two sides play for ninth place in Twickenham next week. Tandy had already teed up making changes in his press duties last week, before confirming he would rotate to face Eddie Jones' side.

Having beaten Japan before the historic win over New Zealand, Wales weren't quite able to get over the line in their third match against Australia - falling just short in a thrilling 29-26 defeat.

However, Tandy will be confident of a repeat victory against Japan - regardless of changes - after Eddie Jones' side conceded 145 points to England and Scotland in the last two weeks.

Naturally, the Wales coach reiterated that it was all about performance, first and foremost.

“We’ve got to build on this and be better than we were this week in terms of our performance," he said. "It’s something we can’t get away from.

“We’ve had a good tournament so far, and we’re disappointed with today. But we want to finish on a high, and that will only be as good as the performance we produce.

“I can rotate the team and we’ll still put in a performance. Ultimately, we’ve got to perform. It doesn’t matter who wears the shirt – we’ve got to perform.

“Whenever we put a team out, the objective is to win a Test match. That will be no different next Saturday.”

Scrum-half Tomos Williams could be one player who doesn't feature next week, having left the field with a groin injury early in the second half.

The Saracens star will be assessed, as Tandy considers changes for next Saturday's match.

“I thought the boys did pretty well," said Tandy. "We’re growing as a team and we’re a young group. Think about where we were 12 months ago.

“The boys have got a couple of days off now, so we’ll look at the changing room and see where we are with injuries.

“We’ll definitely freshen things up for next week.”

Tandy sang the praises of low-cap players like Reuben Morgan-Williams, Kane James and Louie Hennessey - who all came off the bench for solid minutes against Australia.

There could be an opportunity for similarly inexperienced players to get opportunities next week if Tandy does rotate heavily.

Cardiff prop Rhys Barratt, Scarlets wing Macs Page and Dragons duo Che Hope and Aneurin Owen are the uncapped options in the squad.

There are also a handful of players - such as Ellis Mee, Tom Rogers and the recalled Seb Davies - who have yet to feature this autumn.

title: All Blacks equal lowest-ever World Ranking; Northern trio close in on Boks
article_text:
Saturday’s record 37-12 defeat to England in the final round of the pool stages of the Nations Championship has sent New Zealand down to fifth in the World Rugby Men’s Rankings, equalling their lowest-ever position.

New Zealand were last ranked fifth at the end of August 2022, after Argentina inflicted a first-ever home loss on them in Christchurch, 25-18.

Rather than New Zealand, it’s the three strongest teams in the Six Nations who are now breathing down the necks of the Springboks.

Following their 20-17 win over the world champions in Dublin, Ireland have moved up to second on 89.98 points, a gain of two places and 1.28 points. They are 0.47 points ahead of France, who remain in third, but with an improved score of 89.51, after their 45-17 win over Argentina, while England are up one place to fourth, on 89.04 points.

With just 0.74 points separating the Springboks from France, their opponents in next Sunday’s Nations Championship final, the teams are not only playing for the inaugural title but also to finish the year as the world’s No.1 team. Ireland still have a say in that but will get precious few points, if any, for beating the lower-ranked Australia in Friday’s fifth place decider.

The rest of the top 10 is unchanged, but 11th place is now the domain of Japan, who are ranked higher than Italy, following the Azzurri’s home defeat to Fiji.

Meanwhile, Samoa’s forward momentum continues, with a thumping 90-22 Nations Cup win over Spain being rewarded with a two-place rise to 14th. Earlier in the tournament, they were ranked 19th.

The only other major change involves USA, who fall a couple of places to 16th as a result of their 38-10 defeat to fellow Nations Cup champions Georgia.

However, Tonga have swapped places with Spain after they overcame Hong Kong China 55-19, with the Ikale ‘Tahi now 18th and Spain 19th.

title: Springboks issue public denial to Erasmus claims as World Rugby urged to act
article_text:
The Springboks have denied there was any communication between the coaching box and Rassie Erasmus on Saturday - despite the head coach seemingly talking all the way through his watchalong from a Dublin hotel.

Erasmus had been handed a six-match ban in the build-up to the Test match between South Africa and Ireland due to comments he made in the aftermath of defeat to France last weekend. You can read more about that here.

Subsequently, the double World Cup winner was forced to watch events away from the Aviva Stadium, hosting a live watchalong with around 90,000 signed-up supporters. Erasmus spoke briefly before the game and at half-time, but muted the sound on the live stream for the vast majority of the game.

He also appeared to be conversation with someone, but South Africa coach Felix Jones has denied that was the case.

“No, no, I had the mics,” Irishman Jones said, who was reportedly unable to elaborate on the answer as media officers stepped in. “I think Ireland did really well to capitalise off a couple of our exits where we weren’t quite accurate.

“I think we might have given away one or two penalties trying to get out, and Ireland capitalised off it really well and were really accurate with what they did off the back of it, some clever stuff there. I thought they attacked well so full credit to Andrew Goodman, I thought he did a great job.“Then I would say the other area was probably the breakdown, and I felt that they just got a little bit more speed, a little bit quicker in. We were caught sealing a couple of times. I need to watch them back to see why that happened.

“Probably those are the two big ones, but having said that, you know, the Canan Moodie try/no try, he’s in touch... We’d a couple of opportunities right towards the end, with quite a bit of momentum. It was still within our control if we were able to convert, so really close game, but can’t complain.

“I thought Ireland won those key moments that I just mentioned there, and you can see they’re clearly... Andy has a really strong coaching team.

“The breakdown... I know Paul [O’Connell] is all over the breakdown. I know Andrew [Goodman] really well as well. So it’s two really great assistant coaches there, doing a good job.”

Erasmus was not allowed any matchday involvement under the terms of his World Rugby ban - which included coaching, direct or indirect contact with the team management or players, entering the stadium, coaches' box, playing enclosure or technical area.

While it is unclear who Erasmus was communicating with during the game, some fans have suggested World Rugby should investigate if he has breached the terms of his ban.

The coach wore earbuds throughout and leant in behind his laptop while communicating, with his mouth hidden from shot.

He was also seen on his phone several times throughout the game.

title: 'WRU like Man Utd' but Davies backs Faulkner
article_text:
Former Wales captain Jonathan Davies says new Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) chairman Lyndon Faulkner is the man to turn Welsh rugby around.

The former Newport and Pontypool forward, who takes over from Richard Collier-Keywood, attends his first WRU annual general meeting (AGM) on Sunday.

He has already promised to review everything including the controversial plan to cut a men's professional side by 2028.

Faulkner has forged a highly successful business career in the United States of America.

The 66-year-old also has a Welsh rugby background as the nephew of former Wales prop Charlie Faulkner, who was inducted into World Rugby's hall of fame on Saturday alongside Bobby Windsor and Graham Price - the famed Pontypool front row.

Former Wales fly-half Davies, who called for the WRU board to resign before Faulkner's appointment, believes the new chair will galvanise Welsh rugby off the field.

“I believe the chair is a good guy and he has the opportunity to change things and he will make them,” said Davies.

“He is a successful businessman, but he is a rugby man."

Davies has described the problems at the WRU as similar to football giants Manchester United.

“When I look at Manchester United, I also look at the WRU," Davies told BBC Radio 5 Live Sport.

"When United changed and brought the bankers in there was no football knowledge and the same has happened in Welsh rugby."

The former Wales captain said decisions that have been made by the union have been purely financial, and not rugby ones.

“Lyndon is the right man and will make the necessary changes in the WRU to give these guys a better platform," Davies added.

“It’s not going to happen overnight and if we don‘t make these changes we will be in tier two for a long time.”

Davies believes the WRU needs to help the players who earlier this month inspired the nation with a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years, a match played in front of just over 55,000 fans.

“I heard [captain] Dewi Lake say something before the New Zealand game and I felt really sorry for the players," said Davies.

“He said because the attendance was low that was down to them. I felt sad the players felt like that.

“[Welsh rugby] is a real sideshow at the moment with the players taking the brunt of it and Dewi and Jac [Morgan] have gone to Gloucester where, from what I have heard, they have changed the culture and are two great guys.

“Nobody blames the players for where they are, it’s the WRU’s job.

“The New Zealand win shows what the players are capable of, given the right platform.”

Faulkner has also indicated he is a fan of an Anglo-Welsh competition, something with which Davies agrees.

Prem Rugby in England has opened a registration process for teams to apply with the aim of expanding the league to 12 clubs for the 2029-30 season.

Plans to grow the league from the current 10 clubs were confirmed in February, with a 'request for information' stage now open until 1 February 2027.

Clubs, investors and their authorised representatives have been invited to register their interest in joining the English top tier, although a statement said that no formal bid or commitment to invest is required to do so.

The Prem and the Rugby Football Union (RFU) have previously insisted they will consider an English expansion but their press release this week made no mention of only English clubs applying, with Welsh interest in the proposal.

“I think Wales would add to the Prem,” said Davies.

“It’s a brilliant competition already and having Welsh sides in there would benefit Welsh rugby enormously.”

The Prem has consisted of 10 clubs since the 2022-23 season, when Wasps, Worcester and London Irish all folded within the space of a few months.

Promotion and relegation to and from the league was also scrapped as of this season.

Previous conditions said teams would need to compete in the second-tier Champ for a season before being eligible to play in the Prem, and that any bids would be assessed on a range of criteria including finances, investment potential, infrastructure and how their geographical base could help spread the Prem's appeal.

Earlier this month RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney confirmed the WRU had asked to join the Prem and form an Anglo-Welsh league.

Wales currently has four professional sides - Scarlets, Ospreys, Cardiff and Dragons - who play in the United Rugby Championship (URC), although the WRU plans to cut one of the teams by 2028 because of financial issues.

A statement from Prem Rugby and the RFU in October said that the focus was on expanding the league with English clubs although Sweeney confirmed just over a week later that they had been approached by the WRU and that discussions would continue.

The URC has so far not commented on one of its shareholders courting another competition.

The WRU has also not publicly responded to Sweeney's comments about its approach to the RFU but will face questions about the issue at the AGM.

title: All Blacks make Dave Rennie sack decision as coach admits 'we were way worse'
article_text:
Dave Rennie remains under enormous pressure after the All Blacks suffered a humiliating 37-12 defeat to England at Twickenham, but New Zealand Rugby's previous backing of their head coach remains unchanged.

England handed New Zealand their heaviest-ever defeat in the fixture on Saturday, leaving supporters questioning whether Rennie is still the right man for the job.

It was the All Blacks' second successive defeat, having also lost to Wales the previous weekend.

And with the 2027 World Cup less than a year away, the clock is ticking louder than a fire alarm.

New Zealand Rugby had already committed to backing Rennie and his coaching team through to the tournament in Australia.

That support was outlined before Saturday's defeat, rather than being a fresh decision made in its aftermath.

But after another miserable afternoon, plenty of supporters are wondering how much longer that backing can last.

Rennie wasn't interested in making excuses after the final whistle.

Speaking to RUCK at Twickenham, the All Blacks boss admitted his side had taken another backwards step and accepted his share of the blame.

"I'm not going to hide from the fact we weren't good enough and I'm a big part of that," he said.

"Against Wales the only thing we lacked was our finish. Last week I said we let the country down but we were way worse tonight. We need to work out why."

Hardly the words of a man who thinks everything is going swimmingly.

England were stronger, sharper and looked far more organised throughout the contest.

For all New Zealand's talent, they simply had no answer to what Steve Borthwick's side threw at them.

The scale of the defeat was reflected in our All Blacks player ratings, with several big names enduring an afternoon to forget.

And judging by the reaction back home, supporters are running out of patience.

Supporters wasted little time making their feelings known on social media.

One furious fan kept things simple: "Dave Rennie has to resign!"

Another wrote: "It is hard to see how Dave Rennie is going to survive as head coach unless it is a game of two halves."

A third delivered an equally brutal verdict: "2 worst all blacks performances ever."

Others were more concerned by just how easily England appeared to be controlling the contest.

"England are cooking the All Blacks. They're suffocating them and the All Blacks just don't have the answers," one supporter posted.

"Serious questions will be asked of Dave Rennie now."

There was at least one supporter willing to offer Rennie a little sympathy.

"I know the All Blacks are on their way to another test defeat here but at least Dave Rennie is classy, Classy Dave!!"

Unfortunately for Rennie, being a nice bloke doesn't count for much when you're losing Test matches.

For now, Rennie still has the backing of the people who matter.

New Zealand Rugby previously confirmed its support for the head coach and his staff through to the 2027 World Cup.

There has been no confirmed change to that position following the England defeat.

But another heavy loss has hardly strengthened his case.

The All Blacks have now fallen to their joint-lowest world ranking, with England leapfrogging them following Saturday's result.

It is another painful reminder of just how far New Zealand have fallen.

And with the World Cup fast approaching, there is precious little time to put things right.

Changing coaches this close to a World Cup would be a gamble.

But after two successive defeats, sticking with Rennie is beginning to look like one too.

New Zealand Rugby have already made their position clear. Whether they can afford to stick to it is another matter.

title: Wales coach Tandy frustrated by Australia defeat
article_text:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy said he was frustrated as his side failed to back up their epic win over New Zealand, narrowly losing to Australia.

The Wallabies edged the Nations Championship Test 29-26 in Cardiff on Saturday, a week after a first Wales victory over the All Blacks since 1953 had led to wild celebrations.

Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau secured a try-bonus point for Australia as Ryan Lonergan and Carter Gordon added nine points with the boot.

Wales also scored four tries, through Dewi Lake's double, Blair Murray and Ryan Elias, with Sam Costelow landing three conversions.

"The overarching feeling is the frustration of losing," said Tandy.

"We were disappointed. We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been. We were held up three times and could have gone ahead on the scoreboard."

The 46-year-old former Ospreys coach added: "Maybe we needed a little bit of composure but there were enough opportunities to come away with the win.

"I know it's not the result anyone wanted but the supporters were amazing again."

Despite the loss, and that frustration, the Wales head coach praised his side's attitude in attempting to follow up their historic win against the All Blacks.

"Fair play to the boys, after such a monumental game last week with the emotional energy, we stuck in the game and scored four tries," he said.

"So there are a lot of positives in the performance to take as well."

Australia, having soaked up fierce first-half pressure, produced some fine attacking rugby after the break to prevent Wales from winning three matches in a row for the first time since the 2023 World Cup.

"It's sport, you have major highs and then lows, and that's the game we play," said skipper Lake.

"Our frustration comes from the fact that we probably weren't at our best.

"We created opportunities during large parts of the game, but there were little inaccuracies at the wrong times."

Lake, however, said he could not fault the effort of the squad.

"We spoke about backing up last weekend, and we didn't back it up with a result but I think we backed it up with effort and energy," said the captain.

"We had opportunities to win that game, but unfortunately it wasn't to be for us today.

"We'll fix those accuracy issues and we'll be ready to go again next week."

Wales will face Japan at the Allianz Stadium at Twickenham on Saturday (13:10 GMT) after both sides finished fifth in the two Nations Championship tables - north and south.

It will be a fifth time Wales and Japan have met in 16 months with Tandy's side defeating Eddie Jones' team 28-21 in Cardiff just two weeks ago.

Wales have an injury doubt over scrum-half Tomos Williams who has a tight groin, with Tandy expected to make a number changes to freshen up the side.

Australia head coach Les Kiss was happy to have broken a four-match losing sequence which included recent defeats against Scotland and England.

"I am not only proud but also happy for these boys," said Kiss.

"The work they've been putting in over the last four weeks has been good and they just haven't been getting a reward.

"Hats off to Wales. They beat the All Blacks here last week but didn't seem to lack any verve or energy.

"That didn't take it out of them and actually created more energy and confidence in them."

Captain Harry Wilson said it was a special to end the Wallabies' poor sequence.

"When you have four losses on the bounce, you question a few things," said the back-row forward.

"Rugby is such a results-driven game and we hadn't been getting the results even though I felt like we weren't far off last week.

"To beat a team who just had defeated the All Blacks, in front of 65,000 Wales supporters where the atmosphere was crazy, was special."

The Wallabies will now face Ireland on Friday in the contest for fifth place in Twickenham (20:10 GMT) after both sides finished third in their respective pools.

title: Nations Cup wrap: Samoa unleash 13-try blitz and Georgia’s perfect run
article_text:
Former Wallabies centre Irae Simone scored a try on debut for Manu Samoa, who ran away with a 90-22 blitz of Spain in the World Rugby Nations Cup. The 13-try demolition was one of the big talking points from the final round, as Samoa continue to surge up the world rankings.

Pool B champions Georgia hosted the other Nations Cup champions, the USA Eagles, in a round six blockbuster to end the season. Georgia completed a perfect 6-0 unbeaten run throughout the competition as they emerged victorious, 38-10.

Canada, Tonga and Chile also finished the inaugural Nations Cup in the winners’ circle, while Portugal and Uruguay settled for a draw, with their match having to be cancelled due to adverse weather conditions at the Estadio Do Restelo.

Canada and Romania played out an all-time classic to kick off the weekend, with Ben LeSage leading the visitors to a thrilling 27-26 at Stadionul Arcul de Triumf. The Canadians were rewarded with some silverware too, hoisting the Cernavoda Cup post-game.

Tighthead prop Kyle Steeves opened the scoring inside five minutes, with Canada protecting that lead for most of the contest. Romania trailed for 88 per cent of the match, before a late fightback set up a grandstand finish.

Outside back Kyle Tremblay put Canada up 27-12 with about 20 minutes left, before Jean-Pierre Smith hit back for Romania. Canada then went down to 14 men after Matthew Oworu was shown a yellow card, and Romania made the most of their one-man advantage.

Adrian Mitu found the try line with less than five minutes remaining, with the successful Gabriel Rupanu conversion making it a one-point ball game. Romania had 78 per cent possession in the final 10 minutes, but the Canadians hung on for their third Nations Cup win.

Former All Blacks and Hurricanes centre Ngani Laumape debuted for Tonga against Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027-bound Hong Kong China. Laumape started at inside centre and played the full 80 as Tonga claimed a relentless 55-19 win.

Backrower Otunuku Pauta and winger John Tapueluelu scored two tries each, while Siegfried Fisiihoi, Ben Tameifuna, Sam Tuitupou and Taniela Filimone also got on the scoresheet with five-pointers to their name.

Tonga led 33-0 at half-time and never looked back, even though Hong Kong China were produced an improved performance in the second half. But Tonga still ‘won’ the second 40 22-19, with Highlanders-bound first five-eighth Patrick Pellegrini nailing some conversion attempts.

The third match pitted the two Nations Cup winners against one another, with Georgia and the USA already doing enough to wrap up top spot in their pools with one week left. But there was still plenty to play for in Georgia, with both sides going into the match unbeaten.

Georgia went down to 14 men in the 15th minute after Tornike Kakhoidze was sent to the sin bin. Chris Hilsenbeck kicked the USA ahead with a penalty goal four minutes later, before the hosts took control with a barrage of points.

Luka Ivanishvili and Georges Shvelidze scored a try each before the break, before Ivanishvili, Akaki Tabutsadze, Dachi Papunashvili and Akaku Tabutsadze continued the try-scoring bonanza during the second half.

The USA brought an end to that run with 10 minutes left, as backrower Paddy Ryan crashed over the try line for a much-needed score. Following the Hilsenbeck conversion, no more points were scored at Mikheil Meskhi Stadium.

Samoa defeated Spain in the game of the round, with the visitors giving fans plenty to cheer about in their last game of 2026. Spain struggled to hold on as their ill-discipline became a talking point, with the hosts conceding two yellow cards and a red.

Jacob Umaga finished with a 30-point haul, while Theo McFarland topped the carry charts with 13 run, Joel Lam passed the ball 65 times, and Latrell Smilier Ah-Kiong stood out with a game-high nine defenders beaten and five line breaks.

Joel Lam, Ah-Kiong (double), Peter Umaga-Jensen, Lalomilo Lalomilo and Umaga (double) all scored tries for Samoa. Two starting forwards also got on the scoresheet, and Simone was one of the two try-scorers off the bench.

Former Wallaby Simone featured in a Samoan side that included former All Blacks Akira Ioane, Josh Ioane and Shaun Sstevenson. Former Wallaby Scott Sio, who played in the 2015 Rugby World Cup Final, was also named in the run-on side.

Incredibly, Samoa were sitting in 20th spot on the World Rugby rankings at the start of the month, and are now reportedly up to 14th. Spain, meanwhile, played a fair bit of rugby down at least one player, with Gauthier Mingullion receiving a yellow card in the first half and a red in the second.

Chile defeated Zimbabwe 34-29 in the other fixture, with a late comeback from the hosts setting up an exciting finish. Zimbabwe trailed 34-3 at the break, but scored 26 unanswered points in the second half, while Chile briefly went down to 13 men after conceding two yellow cards.

Tyrone Gombe crossed the try line with about one minute left, but time just wasn’t on Zimbabwe’s side, who fell short of what would’ve been a remarkable result. Instead, Chile held on for their fourth Nations Cup win, seeing them finish third in Pool A.

title: Nations Championship finals schedule confirmed as England face All Blacks rematch
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

The line-up for the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend has been confirmed after a thrilling conclusion to pool action.

France will take on South Africa in the inaugural competition decider, with a losing bonus point in Dublin enough for the Springboks to top their group ahead of New Zealand.

The All Blacks will get an immediate opportunity to respond to a record defeat to England, with the two sides meeting again seven days on from a Twickenham thrashing.

Ireland take on Australia, who narrowly squeezed past Wales, with Argentina facing Scotland. Wales against Japan and Italy vs Fiji complete the line-up.

This new competition launched in July pitting the Six Nations sides against the four teams that make-up the Rugby Championship plus Japan and Fiji.

Six games will be held across three days at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium, which has had a new pitch installed in part to deal with the demand of the inaugural finals.

The winner of the decider on Sunday will be crowned the first Nations Championship winners, while a “hemisphere shield” is also up for grabs.

The victor in each game will earn a point for their hemisphere, with the final worth two points to ensure there can be no tie.

Eleventh place final (4.40pm): Italy vs Fiji

Fifth place final (8.10pm): Ireland vs Australia

Ninth place final (1.10pm): Wales vs Japan

Third place final (4.40pm): England vs New Zealand

Seventh place final (1.10pm): Scotland vs Argentina

Nations Championship final (4.40pm): France vs South Africa

title: South Africa coaching staff deny Rassie Erasmus contact during Ireland defeat
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

South Africa’s coaching staff denied suggestions they were receiving instructions from suspended head coach Rassie Erasmus during Saturday’s 20-17 defeat to Ireland in Dublin.

Erasmus, who was barred from any having any involvement in matchday activity as part of his six-game ban from World Rugby, hosted a live watch-along from the team’s hotel.

The 54-year-old was muted for large spells of the online event but could be seen speaking to an unknown party while wearing earbuds and covering his mouth.

Asked if Erasmus was passing on messages, Springboks assistant coach Felix Jones said: “I’ve no idea, we were busy with a Test match.”

Fellow assistant coach Mzwandile Stick added: “Maybe he was communicating with his followers on that party that he was having, but with us we were just in the game.”

Build-up to the heavyweight contest at the Aviva Stadium was dominated by Erasmus being sanctioned after questioning the integrity of match officials following his side’s 21-19 defeat to France.

Jones said the situation was not a distraction as the Springboks slipped to a second successive loss before questions on Erasmus were quickly shut down by the team’s media officer.

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell savoured a “big night for everyone who’s Irish” and a major stepping stone in his side’s journey towards next year’s World Cup.

Robert Baloucoune claimed two first-half tries and Ronan Kelleher added another, with a long-range penalty from Sam Prendergast ultimately proving decisive amid a colossal defensive effort.

“It’s something that we’ve been looking forward to and tried to challenge ourselves with about delivering when it matters against top line sides,” said Farrell.

“We knew that this fixture was coming, playing against the world’s best – world’s best by a stretch at this moment in time, I would have thought so.

“It was a game that we wanted to challenge ourselves and see how we went and obviously fronting up and showing the character that we did and coming out the right side of the win is a big night for everyone who’s Irish.”

South Africa ensured a pulsating encounter remained tantalisingly poised until the final whistle thanks to scores from Morne van den Berg and Malcolm Marx, plus seven points from the boot of Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

“I think we’ve taken a step forward and that was the aim,” said Farrell.

“This game mattered to us in how we prepped for it. We didn’t shy away from that and we took it on for what it was, which was a top of the tree game.

“We were able to perform. It wasn’t perfect but we managed to come out with a win. The World Cup, it’s all about stepping stones and this is a big one that’s for sure.”

Despite their defeat, South Africa progressed to the Nations Championship final at Twickenham after picking up a losing bonus point.

Ireland will likely contest the fifth-place final against either Argentina or Australia.

Asked about Erasmus, Farrell said: “Rassie is his own man and he’s a smart guy. He does things for a reason.

“There’s always going to be a plan or whatever. I don’t know the ins and outs of it.

“The South African boys are in our dressing room having a beer and it’s an unspoken rule that you just leave it alone really I would have thought. It is what it is.”

title: Confirmed Nations Championship Finals Fixtures
article_text:
France will take on South Africa in the inaugural Nations Championship final next Sunday.

After England's emphatic 37-12 victory over New Zealand, France needed to beat Argentina to book their place in the Nations Championship final.

Following a tight first-half, France's quality showed in the second-half as they wrapped up a comfortable 45-17 victory in Paris.

South Africa, who lost 21-19 in France last weekend, suffered a 20-17 loss against Ireland but their losing bonus point was enough to secure top spot in the Southern Hemisphere group.

France and South Africa's progression to the final means that England and New Zealand will meet once again next weekend in a battle for third place.

Elsewhere, Ireland will play Australia in the fifth place final, Scotland take on Argentina for seventh place, Wales face Japan and Italy will come up against Fiji to avoid finishing last.

All six matches will take place at Twickenham and the final between France and South Africa will take place at 16:40 GMT on Sunday afternoon.

title: Ireland pip South Africa in brutal battle to pile more misery on banned Rassie Erasmus
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Ireland celebrated a statement 20-17 win over world champions South Africa at the end of a week dominated by Rassie Erasmus’ suspension saga.

Robert Baloucoune claimed two first-half tries and Ronan Kelleher was also on the scoresheet as Andy Farrell’s side laid down a marker ahead of next year’s World Cup.

Build-up to the heavyweight contest in Dublin centred heavily on Springboks head coach Erasmus being handed a six-match ban after questioning the integrity of match officials following his side’s defeat to France.

His side ensured a pulsating encounter remained tantalisingly poised until the final whistle thanks to scores from Morne van den Berg and Malcolm Marx, plus seven points from the boot of Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

But a long-range penalty from Sam Prendergast, who Erasmus felt should have been banned for this match after his hip-drop tackle against Fiji, ultimately proved decisive.

Both sides finished with 14 players following yellow cards for Ireland captain Dan Sheehan and Springboks replacement Marco van Staden during a breathless finale.

Despite their defeat, South Africa progress to the Nations Champions final at Twickenham after picking up a losing bonus point, while Ireland will almost certainly contest the fifth-place final against either Argentina or Australia.

The Springboks arrived at a sold-out Aviva Stadium without Erasmus, who instead hosted an online watchalong from his team’s hotel.

Erasure’s A Little Respect was among the songs on the pre-game playlist, while some South African supporters in the crowd sported face masks of their absent head coach.

Feinberg-Mngomezulu slotted an early penalty to put South Africa ahead before the hosts hit back when Baloucoune collected Stuart McCloskey’s pass and stepped inside Damian Willemse to dive over.

Roared on by a raucous home crowd, Ireland remained on the front foot.

Baloucoune was denied a second try as he dropped the ball while stretching for the line but atoned two minutes later by again finishing in the right corner, this time from a Mack Hansen pass.

Home fans erupted when Ireland demolished the Springboks’ scrum to win a penalty, before momentum gradually started to shift.

Ireland full-back Hugo Keenan, winning his 50th cap, had to be alert to prevent Springboks replacement Canan Moodie touching down following a fine break from Kurt-Lee Arendse.

However, South Africa’s pressure was eventually rewarded as scrum-half Van den Berg dived under a pile of bodies to score after Ireland’s scrum was overpowered before Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s conversion levelled the scores.

Hooker Kelleher then crashed over from a well-worked line-out at the other end, with Prendergast’s first successful conversion of the evening moving the home team 17-10 in front at the end of an absorbing opening period.

Moodie was denied a try four minutes into the second half by the narrowest of margins as the last-gasp efforts of Hansen were sufficient to push him into touch.

Ireland fly-half Prendergast nervelessly split the posts from distance but Marx bulldozed over and Feinberg-Mngomezulu added the extras to cut South Africa’s deficit to three points.

Sheehan was held up as the home team were denied breathing space. The makeshift number eight was later yellow carded for a dangerous clearout, with Van Staden joining him in the bin following a head hit on Tadhg Beirne.

A heroic defensive effort from Ireland was required to complete the job as the jubilant home crowd revelled in toppling the back-to-back world champions.

title: Maro Itoje head clash sparks All Blacks fury
article_text:
England captain Maro Itoje has sparked a furious reaction from All Blacks supporters after escaping punishment for a controversial head clash during Saturday's showdown at Twickenham.

The incident happened at a breakdown when Itoje appeared to make head-on-head contact with New Zealand forward Tupou Vaa'i.

Vaa'i was left bleeding and required treatment, but the England skipper was not shown a card.

The decision quickly became a major talking point among supporters watching the match.

Several New Zealand supporters questioned why Itoje had escaped punishment, with some arguing that the collision should have resulted in a yellow card.

One fan wrote: "What's that 2 tries and a penalty lol ... 17 points"

Another claimed: "That and the try by Chessum, thought it was a double movement. 2 big plays and no calls."

A third added: "As an unbiased 3rd party, this one absolutely is a penalty and a card and it's really poor the officials missed it."

One supporter defended the decision, writing: "It's accidental head contact in the process of a perfectly normal clear out. Not all head contact is automatically a penalty."

Another insisted there was "nothing wrong with the clear out" and urged supporters to listen to the referee's explanation.

The debate also drew comparisons with the recent controversy surrounding Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus and his criticism of match officials.

One supporter argued there was a difference between fans questioning refereeing decisions and an international coach making allegations about match-fixing.

World Rugby's head-contact framework requires officials to consider the nature of the contact, the level of danger and any mitigating circumstances.

Head-on-head contact does not automatically result in a yellow or red card.

However, the incident involving Itoje has divided supporters, with some convinced the England captain was fortunate to escape punishment.

title: Portugal vs Uruguay Cancelled
article_text:
Saturday’s World Rugby Nations Cup test match between Portugal and Uruguay has been cancelled. Due to climate conditions of a waterlogged field in Lisbon, Portugal, the match officials called off the contest.

According to regulations for the World Rugby Nations Cup, the teams will share the points and thus gain two each. This means Uruguay finish on 14 points and Tonga claim the wooden spoon in Pool A. Portugal finish with 19 competition points to be second to Georgia and five ahead of Spain before Los Leones face Samoa later on Saturday.

The match was to be a very significant contest. It was a dress-rehearsal for Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia, where Portugal and Uruguay compete together in the same pool alongside Ireland and Scotland. The Estádio do Restelo thus offered an early psychological edge ahead of next year’s World Cup showdown but the match was called off.

The match was Uruguay’s last test match before the final preparation stage begins for Rugby World Cup 2027. It is unfortunate for all involved. Of note is that Tomás Batista had been named to debut for Portugal and Alfonso Vidal was set to make his first test start for Los Teros.

title: England hammer New Zealand 37-12 to keep Nations Championship final hopes
article_text:
LONDON, Nov 21 - England thoroughly outplayed New Zealand in a 37-12 win at Twickenham on Saturday as a record victory margin over the All Blacks and a bonus point gave them a chance of making next weekend's Nations Championship final.

The hosts dominated the first half, Henry Slade going over inside five minutes before tries from Jack van Poortvliet and Ben Earl made it 19-0, but Ethan de Groot's try on the cusp of halftime gave the All Blacks hope.

Ollie Chessum powered over for England shortly after the restart, however, and after New Zealand's Beauden Barrett marked his 150th cap with a superb try, Seb Atkinson coasted in to effectively end the contest just after the hour mark.

England's win put them top of the Northern Hemisphere table on 25 points, four ahead of France who host Argentina later on Saturday.

New Zealand remained top of the Southern Hemisphere standings on 22 points, one ahead of South Africa who face Ireland knowing a win would send them into next Sunday's final. REUTERS

title: Superb England run up record win over All Blacks
article_text:
England's revival roared up a gear as they beat New Zealand by a record margin after former captain Lewis Moody led the hosts' response to the haka.

Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year, stood at the centre of a flying V formation that England had adopted for their victories over the same opponents last year and in the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final.

In terms of margin, this win trumped both - and the other seven England victories in the teams' 121-year rivalry.

And the hosts were full value for it. They dominated the All Blacks from the start.

Henry Slade crossed for the opening try in the fourth minute and only England's own mistakes prevented them taking a bigger lead than their 19-5 advantage into the break.

Beauden Barrett marked his 150th Test appearance by rounding off a coast-to-coast Kiwi try to cut England's advantage to 24-12. But his team never really threatened to reel in Steve Borthwick's men.

England introduced five forwards off the bench in the immediate aftermath of that 55th-minute score and, with Ellis Genge in fearsome carrying form, they had more than enough to see out victory in comfort.

Seb Atkinson took a delayed pop pass from Marcus Smith to stroll in for England's fifth try just after the hour.

The hosts finished the game camped down in the New Zealand 22m in search of a sixth score while choruses of Swing Low rolled around the stands.

For New Zealand, who suffered a shock defeat by Wales last weekend, it is a result that suggests a long Test season, which included four Tests against South Africa, may be catching up with them.

By contrast England, who could still end up in next weekend's Nations Championship grand final depending on results, are riding a wave of confidence.

Moody's involvement in the pre-match challenge ensured New Zealand were met by a wall of noise and relentless pressure from kick-off.

Fast starts have become a feature of England's autumn campaign so far, with Australia and Japan both blitzed in the opening minutes.

New Zealand are a class above those teams, but fared little better against the revved-up hosts.

The game was only four minutes old when Slade, with roars from the stands at his back, won the race to a Fin Smith grubber.

After that initial strike, England maintained a stranglehold on the match.

A brilliant 50:22 from George Furbank bought more territory and England, hitting hard in defence, penned New Zealand back.

Their dominance did not immediately translate into points.

Individual errors - Jack van Poortvliet's fumble at the back of a breakdown, Fin Smith's over-cooked cross-field kick, Alex Coles being held up over the line - meant chances went begging.

After half an hour, England had enjoyed 74% of possession, 82% of territory and made 183 metres to New Zealand's 34. A sense the hosts may ultimately regret those mistakes nagged at fans in the stands.

It proved misplaced. Van Poortvliet plunged over from short range after a Cadan Murley break and then, four minutes later, the excellent Ben Earl thundered off the back of a scrum, trampled through Cam Roigard and went under the posts.

New Zealand prop Ethan de Groot burrowed over to repair some of the damage, but at 19-5 down at the break, the visitors were both reeling and somewhat fortunate to still be in touch.

England started the second half at the same breathless pace that marked their approach to the first. Ollie Chessum, lurking out wide, ploughed through the unfortunate Will Jordan for a try inside two minutes of the restart.

Beauden Barrett's score briefly had the embers glowing for New Zealand, but England's bench stomped out any hopes of a comeback.

Genge, Will Stuart, Luke Cowan-Dickie, George Martin and Greg Fisilau gave the forward brought crunching physicality and line speed.

The starters were not far behind, with Chessum levelling former All Black captain Scott Barrett with a superb tackle.

With victory long since secured, an 81,953-strong crowd could relish those individual duels, reflect on a scoreline that exceeded the famous 2012 win and look forward to next weekend, and a possible rematch with New Zealand or meeting with South Africa, at leisure.

title: Scotland score 11 tries in rout of Japan
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Darcy Graham and Liam McConnell inspired acmuch-changed Scotland to a comfortable 11-try 67-5 Nations Championship victory over meek Japan.

Wing Graham moved on to the 41-try mark for his country with a hat-trick as he stepped six clear of Duhan van der Merwe at the top of the national team’s all-time scoring charts.

Back-rower McConnell also enjoyed a day to remember as the 22-year-old back-rower broke his Scotland duck with a treble of his own.

Ollie Smith helped himself to a double while Kyle Rowe, Jamie Dobie and Rory Hutchinson also crossed as the Scots completed their pool-stage fixtures with a fourth win from six matches ahead of their trip to London for finals weekend.

Scotland needed a high-margin victory to have any chance of moving higher than fourth in the Northern Hemisphere table, and – despite Gregor Townsend making 10 changes to the side that started the hard-fought win over Australia last Sunday – they signalled their intent by running in three unanswered tries in the opening quarter.

They got up and running in the sixth minute when Dobie’s high ball was fumbled by the Japanese and Smith hacked the loose ball forward for Graham, who then kicked it on for himself to score.

Tom Jordan, playing at stand-off as talisman Finn Russell was given the weekend off, missed the conversion attempt – the first of four kicks he failed to nail.

The Scots stretched their lead in the 13th minute as McConnell scampered clear to finish on the right after being fed by Smith.

Graham then laid on the third for Rowe in the 20th minute before the Edinburgh wing scored his second of the match on the half hour after faking a pass to McConnell before bundling over the line.

Smith exchanged passes with Rowe before scoring on the left in the 40th minute as the clinical Scots went in leading 29-0 at the break.

McConnell burst away for his second in the 48th minute after more good work by Graham.

The beleaguered Japanese eventually got off the mark in the 53rd minute when Takuro Matsunaga capitalised after a bouncing ball eluded Rowe, but the full-back was unable to add the extras.

The brilliant McConnell bolted clear to complete his hat-trick in the 56th minute before Dobie notched on the left six minutes later.

Smith was presented with an easy finish under the posts for his second of the match in the 67th minute.

Japan were reduced to 14 when hooker Mamoru Harada was sin-binned for a hip drop tackle on Seb Stephen.

Scotland piled on the misery for Eddie Jones’ side by claiming a further two tries in the closing stages from Hutchinson and Graham, either side of another yellow card for Michael Stolberg.

title: Portugal versus Uruguay World Rugby's Nations Cup match in Lisbon canned
article_text:
Portugal’s World Rugby Nations Cup clash with Uruguay in Lisbon has been effectively been rained off.

Portugal sit second in the Pool 2, while Uruguay sit sixth of six in the Pool 1.

A World Rugby statement reads: “Today’s World Rugby Nations Cup 2026 match between Portugal and Uruguay, scheduled for 15:00 at Estadio do Restelo in Lisbon, has been cancelled due to a waterlogged pitch and further heavy rain forecast.

“Match officials, in consultation with both teams, made the decision following pitch inspections that confirmed conditions were unplayable and unsafe.

“The match has been declared a draw, with each team awarded two competition points.”

Elsewhere, Tonga showed their class to easily beat Hong Kong China 55-19, while Canada won away 27-26 to Romania in Bucharest on Friday.

title: Ex-captain Moody joins England in emotional haka response
article_text:
Former England captain Lewis Moody joined the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium.

Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge.

Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks.

Moody, who was embraced by most of England's team in the aftermath of the challenge and its acceptance, also delivered the match ball.

With Twickenham energised, England started the match fast, with Henry Slade getting on the end of a Fin Smith grubber kick to score the first try after just four minutes.

All of England's players are wearing boots emblazoned with the logo of Moody's Front Up to MND campaign, to which signed warm-up and match-worn shirts will be donated.

The campaign's first fundraising drive is a mass-participation coastal walk in June, which aims to raise more than £1m to fund research into the disease.

A statement from England Rugby said: "As a hugely respected former England captain, it was important to the England men's team to show their support for Lewis and to involve him in many areas of the match day, including on the pitch.

"Supporting Lewis and Front Up reflects the game's commitment to standing alongside those affected by MND, and to help raise awareness and funds for research."

Moody delivered the match ball before England's victory over Australia last autumn, a few weeks after he revealed his diagnosis in an interview with BBC Breakfast.

Last weekend, Wales players were bathed in red light and smoke during the All Blacks' haka in a response that was 'a year in the making'.

title: England set for ANOTHER World Rugby fine after epic All Blacks haka response
article_text:
Steve Borthwick's side recreated their famous V-shaped formation from the 2019 Rugby World Cup, with England legend Lewis Moody leading the response.

The 2003 World Cup winner stood at the front as Maro Itoje and his teammates spread across the pitch to face New Zealand's traditional challenge.

It was an emotional moment for Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) in September 2025.

The former England captain was helping launch his new Front Up to MND campaign, which aims to raise money for research into the disease.

England's players also showed their support by wearing specially designed boots and training tops promoting the campaign.

However, amid the incredible atmosphere, two England stars may have landed the RFU in hot water.

Ollie Chessum and Jamie George appeared to cross the halfway line during the haka, something prohibited under World Rugby's protocol for cultural challenges.

The pair's actions could now leave England facing another financial penalty.

Under the protocol, players receiving the haka must remain in their own half of the pitch.

England have already been punished for doing exactly the same thing.

World Rugby has yet to announce whether any disciplinary action will follow Saturday's incident.

Why was Lewis Moody leading England's haka response?

The 48-year-old has joined forces with the My Name'5 Doddie Foundation, established in honour of the late Scotland legend Doddie Weir.

His latest fundraising challenge will see supporters take part in coastal walks across the UK on 12 June 2027.

Moody hopes the campaign will help fund research into treatments and ultimately a cure for MND.

Speaking about the campaign, he said: "There's no question MND is the greatest challenge yet."

He added: "I have a platform to try to help all those living with MND and I'm determined to use it to make the maximum impact I possibly can."

Supporters can learn more and get involved through Front Up to MND.

title: England pull Lion from squad moments before All Blacks clash

title: England vs All Blacks referee accused Rassie Erasmus of damaging his reputation
article_text:
Australian referee Nic Berry will take charge of England’s clash with the All Blacks this weekend, but his appointment brings back memories of one of rugby’s biggest officiating controversies.

Berry was at the centre of a high-profile dispute with Springboks director of rugby Rassie Erasmus in 2021, which ultimately resulted in the South African receiving a two-month suspension.

The Australian will be the man in the middle at Allianz Stadium, with the result set to have major implications for the Nations Championship table as both sides look to finish top of their respective hemispheres.

A former professional rugby player, Berry represented the Queensland Reds, Racing Métro and London Wasps before retiring in 2012 following a series of concussions.

He turned to refereeing in 2015 and quickly climbed the ranks, making his Super Rugby debut a year later before taking charge of matches at the 2019 and 2023 Rugby World Cups.

However, his appointment will bring back memories of the first Lions Test in Cape Town on 24 July 2021.

Berry refereed the encounter, which saw the British & Irish Lions claim a 22-17 victory over South Africa.

In the aftermath, Erasmus released a 62-minute video highlighting 26 incidents in which he believed Berry had made incorrect or inconsistent decisions.

The video questioned several calls, including those involving Springboks captain Siya Kolisi and Lions skipper Alun Wyn Jones.

Berry later accused Erasmus of carrying out a public character assassination and damaging his professional reputation.

World Rugby subsequently found the South African guilty of six counts of misconduct, handing him a two-month suspension from all rugby activities and an additional match-day ban. SA Rugby was also fined £20,000.

Berry later revealed how difficult the ordeal had been for both himself and his family.

Erasmus eventually apologised for his actions, but the incident remains one of the most significant controversies of Berry’s refereeing career.

It also provides some added context to this weekend’s appointment, particularly given that Erasmus has once again found himself suspended after criticising match officials, this time following South Africa’s 21-19 defeat to France on Friday.

He received a six-match ban over his comments.

title: Why Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus is serving World Rugby ban in hotel room
article_text:
Ireland and South Africa lock horns at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday afternoon in one of the standout fixtures of the year - but one important man will be very noticeable by his absence.

Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus won't be in attendance, instead watching events from a Dublin hotel room.

The double World Cup winner has been banned for six matches by the sport's governing body World Rugby because of comments he made in a press conference at the start of the week.

In an extraordinary media session with journalists, Erasmus reflected on the world champions' defeat to France in Paris last week, claiming officials had missed 17 knee-drop tackles on his players, suggesting acts of foul play were not being picked up in what he called a "manipulation of the game", before adding that he felt referees were showing more leniency to sides from the northern hemisphere.

He also questioned whether referees missing offences could be "match-fixing", a comment which is likely to have triggered World Rugby's probe into his rant.

They acted swiftly, banning the head coach from the next six games, which includes today's clash against Andy Farrell's men and the Nations Championship finals day at Allianz Stadium Twickenham next weekend. You can read World Rugby's lengthy statement here.

The Springboks responded with a statement of their own, requesting a personal hearing.

The statement read: “SA Rugby is requesting a full misconduct hearing for Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus following his sanctioning by an independent World Rugby panel for comments made in a press conference in Dublin on Monday.

“A SA Rugby spokesperson said that the organisation respected the process but had requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives.

“SA Rugby trusted that such a hearing could be expedited considering the seriousness of the charge, and will not make any further comment until the hearing could be completed.”

At the time of writing, that hearing is yet to take place.

Following on from his ban, Erasmus took to social media to invite supporters to watch the match against Ireland along with him from his hotel room using a new website, watchwithrassie.com, where they can sign up to take part.

"Can sit and moan or make the best of it," he wrote on X.

"I'll be watching the match at the hotel. Not keen to watch [it] on my own.

"So, let's give it a go and hope I get the 'tech' sorted = TV on, My Laptop camera on, and you're welcome to join me."

He has since been hit with the threat of breaching media rights should he feature live match footage in his broadcast.

title: England fined by World Rugby following controversial All Blacks haka response
article_text:
England face the All Blacks this weekend, with plenty of intrigue surrounding how Steve Borthwick's side will respond to the haka following Wales' remarkable pre-match display last weekend.

The Welsh Rugby Union paid tribute to the iconic 1905 encounter between the two nations, when Wales famously answered the All Blacks' challenge by singing the Welsh National Anthem at Cardiff Arms Park.

The latest presentation offered a modern twist on one of rugby's most enduring traditions.

As the stadium lights dimmed, New Zealand stood beneath a single spotlight to perform their haka, commanding the attention of the crowd.

Wales then delivered their response. Illuminated by a deep red backlight and surrounded by smoke, the home side created a striking visual display that the Welsh Rugby Union dubbed 'Dragon's Breath'.

Red lighting swept across the stadium as Steve Tandy's players stood together, delivering a powerful response to the New Zealand challenge.

They went on to achieve something Wales had not managed since 1953, securing a historic victory over the All Blacks.

England, meanwhile, have their own history when it comes to responding to the haka, having previously found themselves in trouble with World Rugby.

The most memorable example came in the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final in Yokohama. As New Zealand began their traditional challenge, Owen Farrell's England refused to stand back and watch.

Instead, they broke protocol by advancing into a bold V-shaped formation, spreading across the pitch.

Several players, including Joe Marler, Ben Youngs, Elliot Daly, Billy Vunipola, Luke Cowan-Dickie and Mark Wilson, even stepped into New Zealand's half.

Referee Nigel Owens was forced to intervene and order the England players back, while World Rugby later handed the RFU a £2,000 fine for breaching the rules surrounding responses to the haka.

However, Eddie Jones' side had the last laugh on the pitch, producing a 19-7 victory to book their place in the World Cup final.

Six years later, England revived the tactic ahead of another meeting with the All Blacks, bringing back the famous V formation.

This time, Henry Pollock and Jamie George were among those leading the response, with 20-year-old Pollock also catching the eye as he licked his lips while 'Swing Low, Sweet Chariot' rang around the stadium during the haka.

Once again, England backed up the pre-match theatre with a performance to match.

After falling 12-0 behind early on, Borthwick's side fought back to score four tries and claim an impressive victory over the world's second-ranked team.

According to Borthwick, much of the motivation came from an impassioned pre-match address by captain Maro Itoje, which helped set the tone for the afternoon.

Victory over New Zealand is crucial if they are to keep their hopes of finishing top of the northern hemisphere table in the inaugural Nations Championship alive and secure a place in the final.

title: Only one nation offered Rassie Erasmus support after six-match ban
article_text:
Japan head coach Eddie Jones has emerged as the only rival international boss to offer Rassie Erasmus any real sympathy following his controversial six-match suspension.

The Springboks coach was punished by World Rugby after questioning the officiating during South Africa's 21-19 defeat to France.

Erasmus highlighted a series of alleged illegal tackles before suggesting the failure to penalise them could amount to manipulation of the game.

While several leading coaches have defended match officials or refused to comment, Jones took a different approach.

Writing in his Daily Mail column, the former England boss revealed he had contacted Erasmus personally.

Jones said he believed the South African had legitimate concerns about decisions made during the defeat in Paris.

He even sent Erasmus a private text message expressing his support for those concerns.

However, Jones made clear that his sympathy had limits.

As Sky Sports reported, he believed the Springboks coach had gone too far by raising the possibility of match-fixing.

Jones also questioned whether World Rugby treats every nation equally, suggesting some countries receive preferential treatment.

The comments add another twist to the controversy surrounding Erasmus, whose suspension has already forced him to make alternative plans to watch South Africa face Ireland.

The response from other international coaches has been noticeably different.

England boss Steve Borthwick defended match officials, insisting they deserve respect and expressing complete confidence in their integrity.

France coach Fabien Galthié also stressed the responsibility coaches have to protect referees.

Ireland's Andy Farrell refused to discuss the controversy ahead of Saturday's clash with South Africa.

Scotland boss Gregor Townsend similarly avoided offering an opinion, joking about whether Erasmus was a Japanese player.

All Blacks coach Dave Rennie expressed sympathy for officials dealing with increasingly complicated tackle laws, although he did not directly address Erasmus's suspension.

That leaves Jones as the only rival head coach to have publicly offered meaningful sympathy for Erasmus's complaints.

Erasmus will be absent from the Aviva Stadium when South Africa face Ireland in the Nations Championship.

The suspension also prevents him from attending the finals weekend later this month.

However, the Springboks boss has already announced plans to host a live watchalong from his hotel.

Jones has even suggested he might tune in.
