Carlos Alcaraz makes ‘frustrated’ admission after beating Ben Shelton at ATP Finals
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has shared his thoughts after reaching the final at the 2026 ATP Finals with a comeback victory against Ben Shelton.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion defeated world No 4 Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) in the semi-finals at the season-ending championships in Turin on Saturday.

Alcaraz finished top of the John McEnroe Group at the ATP Finals with a 3-0 record after he did not drop a set in dominant wins over Frances Tiafoe, Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli.

The world No 3 lost his serve for the first time in the tournament in the second game against Shelton, and he was unable to break back in the opening set.

The Spanish star responded strongly in the second set, and he broke the big-serving American at 4-3 before holding serve to force a decider.

Neither player faced a break point in the third set, but Alcaraz sealed the win in style as he dominated the decisive tiebreak by winning the last seven points.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Alcaraz now holds a 5-1 record against Shelton, having beaten the American in the Paris Masters final earlier this month after losing the pair’s epic quarter-final at the 2026 US Open.

In his on-court interview with Tennis TV, Alcaraz admitted he was frustrated by how he started the match.

“Well, just really, really happy. I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn’t start the match the way I wanted to, to be honest,” said the 23-year-old.

“And against someone like Ben; big serve, big… playing from the baseline, I think he just pushes you to the limit every time. And I think I just didn’t start that well.

“And then the break early, it was tough for me to deal with. But I’m just happy that I came back in the second set playing such a great tennis. Step by step, focus on my things, and ended up playing a good tennis.

“I think the third set was even closer, I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set; myself, as well.

“Great points, great games, and just happy to play a great tennis in the tiebreak — I think it’s when it matters, to be honest.

“So, excited for tomorrow and happy with everything today.”

Alcaraz will face either Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev in the final in Turin on Sunday. He is aiming to win his maiden ATP Finals title.

title: “I feel great but don’t have to push myself to the limit”: Alcaraz passes his hamstring test, but is learning not to chase every ball
article_text:
After beating Ben Shelton in the ATP Finals semi-finals in Turin on Saturday, two days after an MRI on his hamstring, Carlos Alcaraz said the match was “a great feedback” on his physical state. The Spaniard admits he is still holding back on some movements ahead of Sunday’s final.

Carlos Alcaraz feels good enough to play for the title. “Today again, a really important test for myself to see where I am physically,” the Spaniard said on Saturday in Turin, after beating Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) to reach the ATP Finals final, two days after an MRI on his hamstring. “I think it went great. I feel great, moving hard, probably not pushing myself to the limit.”

Asked how he felt after two hours of intense battle, and about the strapping visible on his leg, he admitted he is still managing the problem. “Probably without this problem in the leg I could move differently a little bit, probably even harder, but I’m realizing that I just need to be careful with it, and sometimes I don’t have to push myself to the limit in some movements (…) and some balls. I don’t have to run every ball, which I’m just understanding right now.”

“I’m feeling better, feeling good. Today was a great feedback for me,” he added. “Right now I’m going to (…) try to recover and be ready for tomorrow.”

In Spanish, he went a step further, explaining that the injury had taught him something about the way he plays. “Physically, I felt very good. It wasn’t a moment for doubts (…). Honestly, I felt good. Maybe I didn’t go crazy the way I might have done at another time if I hadn’t had the leg issue, but I think this has also helped me understand a little how I should go for a lot of balls when I’m healthy: maybe I don’t have to go crazy, I don’t have to run for certain impossible balls to be well physically,” he said. “Now we are going to use every minute and every hour of the day to recover, to do things right and to be as good as possible tomorrow.”

On court, the hamstring did not stop him from raising his level when it mattered, winning the third-set tie-break 7-1. “Today I just went for it, to be honest. I didn’t think about physically. I just felt well, and if I lose, it was totally fair,” Alcaraz said.

He described the mindset he took into that tie-break. “I don’t try anything different. I just try to play a good tennis, and I try not to let the moment affect my game, affect myself. I just try to be calm, I try to be relaxed and try to do the things that I have to do,” he said. “If I miss, if I lose, but feel like I did the right things, I’m leaving the court happy and I’m proud. So it wasn’t about being nervous about that moment, it’s just about to accept it, to enjoy playing this moment.”

The Spaniard had cancelled his practice on Thursday after the MRI and beaten Flavio Cobolli on Friday while deliberately holding back physically. He has never revealed his diagnosis. On Sunday, he will play for the title against the winner of the evening’s semi-final between Alexander Zverev and Daniil Medvedev, a year after losing the final to Jannik Sinner.

title: Carlos Alcaraz: Seven-time Grand Slam champion sinks Ben Shelton to reach championship match at ATP Finals
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz made it a lucky 13 wins in a row against Ben Shelton to reach Sunday's showpiece of the ATP Finals in Turin.

Alcaraz, who eased concerns about a hamstring injury by completing an unbeaten group-stage campaign, defeated American third seed Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1) despite heavy strapping on his upper left leg.

The Spaniard was beaten by Jannik Sinner in last year's final in Turin but will be determined to go one better this time around and claim his first year-end title. He will face either Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev in Sunday's championship match.

title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s ranking points & prize money after ATP Finals semi-final
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz prevailed in a deciding set tiebreak to defeat Ben Shelton in a pulsating semi-final at the 2026 ATP Finals.

World No 3 Alcaraz fought back to earn a 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) victory over fourth-ranked Shelton in the last four at the Inalpi Arena in Turin.

The Spanish star produced a stunning level to seal the win as he dominated the third set tiebreak by winning the last seven points of the match.

Alcaraz, who is chasing his maiden ATP Finals title, is through to his second final at the season-ending championships, having lost to Jannik Sinner in last year’s title match.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion dismantled Frances Tiafoe, Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli in the round robin stage in Turin, and he has extended his overall winning streak to 13 matches.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Shelton was playing his first semi-final at the ATP Finals in what was his second appearance at the prestigious indoor hard-court event after he made his debut in 2025.

The American progressed to the last four after winning two of his three matches in the group stage.

Alcaraz has earned 400 ATP ranking points for his semi-final win against Shelton, having already collected 600 points for his three round robin wins.

Shelton defeated Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar in his first and third matches in the John McEnroe Group either side of a loss to Alexander Zverev.

The US Open finalist secured 400 ranking points for his two victories in Turin.

Alcaraz has collected a $2,759,000 for his unbeaten run to the final in Turin, and he could take his prize money haul to $5,171,000 if he lifts the trophy.

Shelton has earned $1,148,000 for his campaign at the ATP Finals.

Lakshya Sen's title hat-trick bid ends as Satwik-Chirag also crash out, India draw blank at Hong Kong Ope

Lakshya's bid for a third consecutive title was halted by Denmark's Anders Antonsen, who produced a commanding 21-13, 21-13 victory. Earlier, Satwik and Chirag, the world No. 6 pair, went down 18-21, 19-21 against Malaysia's eighth-seeded combination of Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun.

The defeats meant India finished the tournament without a finalist, despite Lakshya arriving in Hong Kong on the back of consecutive titles at the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan over the last two weeks.

Satwik and Chirag began their semifinal with a 4-1 head-to-head advantage over Man and Tee, but the Malaysians proved more effective in the crucial moments.

The Indians made an encouraging start, racing to a 3-0 lead, before their opponents fought back in an attacking contest featuring sharp returns, angled shots and powerful smashes.

The scores remained close through the opening exchanges, but Man and Tee edged ahead 11-10 at the interval.

Tee then raised his intensity as the Malaysians opened up a 16-12 lead.

Satwik and Chirag fought back from 16-19 to level at 19-19 in the second game after trailing 15-18, but the Malaysians held their nerve. They targeted Chirag to earn match point before sealing the contest with a precise push into the corner.

The defeat ended another impressive season for the Indian pair, who had won titles in Singapore and China this year.

Lakshya, meanwhile, struggled to find his rhythm against Antonsen, who controlled the rallies with accurate placement and clever angles.

The Danish shuttler established an early 3-0 lead before Lakshya fought back to make it 8-8. However, Antonsen moved ahead at the interval and gradually took control, closing out the opening game 21-13.

The second game followed a similar pattern. Antonsen moved ahead 5-2 after the change of ends and carried an 11-6 advantage into the interval.

Lakshya produced occasional moments of resistance but remained inconsistent, allowing Antonsen to extend his lead to 18-9. The Dane eventually converted his third match point to complete a comfortable victory.

Lakshya's movement and reactions appeared a fraction slower, with the accumulated workload of his recent title-winning run possibly catching up with him.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026 badminton: Lakshya Sen's 13-match winning streak ends in semi-finals
Hong Kong Open: ‘We Will Come Back Stronger’
article_text:
Goh Soon Huat and Lai Shevon Jemie came to LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 needing a miracle – and very nearly pulled it off.

Having suffered three first-round exits in their previous four tournaments, the Malaysian husband-and-wife duo hauled themselves off the canvas and back into the race for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 with a gritty semifinal run. Standing between them and the final ticket to Hangzhou next month were top seeds Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dong Ping.

On Saturday, Goh and Lai pushed the Chinese powerhouse to the brink before falling 21-17 21-18 – a result that officially wrapped up the mixed doubles qualification race and handed the last berth to Japanese pair Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi.

Yet, despite the heartbreak of falling short of a season-finale appearance, there were no hung heads in the mixed zone. Instead, there was a quiet, hard-earned relief their spark had returned.

“It wasn’t a perfect match but both of us gave the best we had,” said Lai. “Coming in from quite a rollercoaster of results and performances, today was one of our steadier matches. Although we didn’t manage to get the win, we did quite well.”

They certainly made Feng and Huang sweat, clawing back in the second game to snatch a 16-15 lead before the world No.1s slammed the door shut.

“Against the Chinese pairs, even if you lead by quite a few points, it’s still not much of an advantage because they have the ability to catch right back up,” Lai admitted.

Goh echoed that sentiment, confessing that the weight of the occasion briefly got the better of his footwork. “At the start, I quite enjoyed the match. But once we reached a more crucial point, I began to put more pressure on myself and lost my pacing – my speed got too fast and broke my rhythm.”

Still, as their 2026 campaign ends, the detour to Hong Kong proved invaluable.

“The good thing is we have regained our momentum, our rhythm and most importantly, our confidence,” Goh noted.

For Lai, who openly admitted she had been battling self-doubt, the semifinal run was the exact validation she needed.

“I can see the results of my training showing up on court this time,” she said. “That has given me a good push to know I’m heading in the right direction.”

Hangzhou will have to wait, then – but with their mojo firmly back in their kit bags, Goh and Lai are already looking forward to what 2027 brings.

title: 2026 WTA Rankings Winners & Losers: Elena Rybakina +4, Iga Swiatek -7, Alex Eala +38, Emma Raducanu -79
article_text:
The 2026 WTA Tour season has wrapped up and there is a new No 1 as Elena Rybakina finished at the top of a different-looking top-20 in the WTA Rankings compared to the start of the year.

Rybakina started the 2026 campaign at No 5 in the rankings, but she took over at No 1 after the US Open in September and confirmed her position as year-end No 1 during the Asian swing, bringing an end to Aryna Sabalenka’s long reign.

And there is also a new No 2 with teenager Mirra Andreeva finishing at a career-high on the back of her French Open and WTA Finals titles this year, up from No 9 last year.

Sabalenka – who started the year at No 1 and spent 99 consecutive weeks at the top – finishes at No 3.

The Sabalenka-Iga Swiatek days of dominance ended this year as the latter was No 2 on January 1, but she slipped to No 9 with neither winning a Grand Slam in 2026 although the Belarusian finished runner-up to Rybakina at the Australian Open and US Open.

Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula are still firmly part of the top 10, but the likes of Madison Keys (-12), Amanda Anisimova and Jasmine Paolini (-27) have dropped off.

Elina Svitolina (+8), Linda Noskova (+6), Karolina Muchova (+11) and Marta Kostyuk (+16) have moved into the top 10.

In terms of those who finished between No 11 and No 20 in 2026, Maja Chwalinska was at No 150 on 1 January and finds herself 138 places higher at No 12 with her rise coming on the back of her runners-up finish at Roland Garros and her maiden WTA 1000 title at the Wuhan Open.

No 13 Iva Jovic is +22 thanks to a run to the quarter-finals at the Australian Open and the successful defence of her WTA 500 trophy at the Guadalajara Open.

Fellow rising star Alex Eala sits two places behind the American as she climbed 38 places from No 53 with her jump coming on the back of her maiden WTA Tour title at the WTA 500 Washington DC Open while she also finished runner-up at the Hong Kong WTA 250 event.

Sorana Cirstea is up from No 43 to No 16 as she finished her final year as a professional with the Transylvania Open title and a quarter-final appearance at Roland Garros.

*Although the WTA Tour season is over, there are still a few WTA 125K and ITF events taking place, but no one in the top 20 will feature so the above top 20 will remain unchanged, while there could be one or two changes lower down the list.

Kristina Liutova started the 2025 season at No 714, but the 16-year-old surged up the rankings on the back of her maiden title at the Memphis Classic as she became the second youngest player to win a WTA Tour title on debut.

The Russian teenager is currently at No 103, 611 places better off than on 1 January.

Sara Bejlek, Lilli Tagger, Diane Parry, Claire Liu and Hariet Dart also won their maiden titles this year and also earned big jumps.

Czech Bejlek sits at No 33, having started the year at No 92, Parry is one place behind her after surging 90 spots from No 124, Tagger won her maiden title at the age of 18 and she rose from No 159 to No 54, while Liu is +140 from No 207 to No 67 and Dart is +87 from No 172 to No 85.

Dart is currently the British No 3 behind Katie Boulter – who started 2026 at No 106, but is currently No 50 – and Sonay Kartal (No 68 to No 54).

Former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin’s struggles continued in 2026 as she started at No 28, but has dropped 161 places to no 189.

Emma Raducanu finished the 2025 season as the British No 1 as she was No 29 and she reached No 23 in March, but injury ruined her year as she didn’t play any matches during the second half of the campaign and has slumped 79 places to No 108.

title: Iga Swiatek makes huge schedule change as first event of 2027 season confirmed
article_text:
Iga Swiatek will not line up at the 2027 United Cup as she has opted not to compete at the annual team tournament for the first time since its launch, instead signing up for a regular WTA Tour event.

Since the inaugural United Cup in 2023, Swiatek has been an ever-present member of Team Poland and steered them to back-to-back runners-up titles in 2024 and 2025 before they finally got their hands on the coveted winner’s trophy last year.

But the six-time Grand Slam winner won’t be part of Poland’s title defence in January 2027 as she has decided to swap the team environment for the individual competition of the Tour by entering the Brisbane International.

Swiatek will make her debut at the WTA 500 event that will also feature world No 1 Elena Rybakina – who won the title in 2024 – and four-time Grand Slam winner Naomi Osaka.

Aryna Sabalenka won the tournament the past two years, but organisers are yet to confirm if she will return to seek a third consecutive trophy at the season opener.

For Swiatek, it is certainly a big shift in her calendar following a disappointing 2026 season that saw her fail to win a Grand Slam for the first time since 2021. Her best run at the majors was at the Australian Open where she reached the quarter-finals.

Although she won two titles – the United Cup and the Canadian Open – she finished a disappointing ninth in the WTA Rankings, having started the year at No 2 behind Sabalenka, as she failed to qualify for the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

The last time the former world No 1 finished that lowly was back in 2021.

There is no doubt that she and her team, with coach Francisco Roig leading the way, hopes this change will lead to a better 2027 season, especially with several high-quality opponents set to test her in Brisbane ahead of the first Grand Slam of the year.

Before signing up for the United Cup, Swiatek competed at the 2022 Adelaide International and reached the semi-final before losing against then world No 1 Ashleigh Barty. That, though, gave her confidence ahead of the Australian Open as she also reached the last four in Melbourne, but lost against Danielle Collins.

In 2021, she started at the Gippsland Trophy and made it to the quarter-finals, while in 2020 and 2019 she kicked off her season at the Australian Open.

Andy Murray: Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes Scot will one day take the role
article_text:
Great Britain's outgoing Davis Cup captain Leon Smith hopes "standout candidate" Andy Murray will one day take the role he is vacating after more than 16 years.

Smith took over from John Lloyd in 2010 following a humiliating loss to Lithuania that left Britain facing relegation to the bottom level of the historic competition.

Harnessing the talents and commitment of Murray, who he coached as a junior, Smith led Britain back to the top tier and, only five years later, to a first title since 1936 when they defeated Belgium in 2015.

Murray won all 11 singles and doubles rubbers he contested in 2015, as well as 33 out of 36 in singles in the competition overall.

The 39-year-old, who is currently head coach to Jack Draper, paid tribute to Smith, saying: "Winning the Davis Cup in 2015 with Leon as captain was one of the proudest moments of my career.

"He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play.

"I've obviously known Leon a long time, since he coached me as a kid. I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench.

"I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain."

Smith, whose final tournament will be next week's Finals in Bologna, where Great Britain face Germany in the quarter-finals, hopes Murray will one day take the role.

"I think it is timing for him, he's busy with his life," Smith said. "He obviously is the standout candidate, isn't he? For all the attributes and more.

"Hopefully it's something he's interested in the future.

"The Davis Cup, it's not just the ties itself. It's being at the events. It's supporting the players and their personal coaches on their journeys.

"And it's also the Olympics and his history in the Olympics is second to none.

"So I do hope it's something he does in the future, but I respect that it's not for him right now, and I can understand it.

"But I really hope at some point in the future that he does take it on."

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis, Andy's older brother Jamie discussed the role with Gigi Salmon and Tim Henman.

The seven-time Grand Slam doubles champion said: "I think that's an interesting way to see how they're going to go about it. I think there's probably quite a few people that would quite fancy it.

"I think Greg [Rusedski] as well, with everything that he's done in his career, would definitely deserve to be in that conversation.

"I'm sure Andy will get asked about his interest levels. He certainly should be given everything that he's done for tennis in our country."

Henman reflected on Smith's tenure by saying: "A big part of that role was making sure that Andy turned up to play and then giving him the environment to go out and perform as well as he could.

"Andy at that time was loving playing Davis Cup, representing his country and the team went from strength to strength.

"When Leon started, they were at the bottom of professional tennis, but they worked their way up to lifting the trophy in Belgium."

title: Wang Zhiyi and Tomoka Miyazaki vie for Hong Kong Open title without Ahn
article_text:
A showdown between the top players from China and Japan will decide who takes the crown at the Hong Kong Open, with badminton world No. 1 Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) absent.

World No. 3 Wang Zhiyi and No. 7 Tomoka Miyazaki will meet in the Hong Kong Open semifinals. Both are set for a must-win battle as they pursue a place in the final and the title.

Wang Zhiyi and Miyazaki both won their women's singles quarterfinals on the 20th at the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500) at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong, securing places in the semifinals.

Wang Zhiyi was first to reach the semifinals after a hard-fought match. She beat Indonesia's Putri Kusuma Wardani, ranked No. 9 in the world, 2-0 (22-20, 22-20). Both games went to deuce at 20-20, but Wang stayed focused at the decisive moments and closed out the match with consecutive points.

The win was also significant because Wang was the last Chinese woman left in the singles draw. Tokyo Olympic gold medalist Chen Yufei, ranked No. 4 in the world, lost to India's Santoshi Ramraj, while Han Yue and Su Wenjing were also eliminated. Wang was the only Chinese player left, preserving her country's pride.

Miyazaki also secured a semifinal berth with a dominant performance. She routed fellow Japanese player Hina Akechi, ranked No. 14 in the world, 2-0 (21-11, 21-9). After coming back from an early deficit in the first game, she extended her lead with a run of points. She then put Akechi under pressure from the start of the second game and won comfortably.

The victory also served as revenge for Miyazaki. She put behind her a painful 2-1 comeback loss to Akechi in the Korea Open quarterfinals on the 6th in Yeosu, South Jeolla province.

The two players will now face off for a place in the final. Wang remains China's only hope in women's singles, while Miyazaki has an opportunity to prove herself as the next ace of Japanese women's badminton.

The title race has become more competitive with world No. 1 Ahn Se-young (Samsung Life Insurance), No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi of Japan and No. 5 Pusarla Venkata Sindhu of India all absent from the tournament. With the dominant favorite out, Wang and Miyazaki have emerged as title contenders.

Wang has shown her determination to reclaim the title, surviving to the semifinals as the only Chinese player left in the tournament. Miyazaki has already secured a spot in the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals and is determined to keep her momentum going with a title win ahead of the season-ending event.

If both players win their semifinals, they will advance to the final, where they will be just one match away from the title. With Ahn absent from the Hong Kong Open, attention is focused on whether China's Wang will challenge for the title or Japan's Miyazaki will emerge as the new queen.

title: Alcaraz puts aside injury concerns to take apart Cobolli
article_text:
A ruthless Carlos Alcaraz put aside his injury concerns to dismantle Flavio Cobolli and ensure a perfect record in the ATP Finals group stages.

Spain's Alcaraz hurt his left hamstring in his previous match against Daniil Medvedev and had a scan on the injury on Thursday.

He arrived for his match against Cobolli with strapping on his upper-left leg - as well as tape on his right knee and a sleeve on his right arm - but was brutally efficient in a 6-4 6-1 win.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion did not face a break point and bludgeoned 29 winners in a 65-minute victory.

"I tried not to move that much. I tried to be aggressive, to dominate the match as much as I can," the 23-year-old said.

"I'm just really happy that I am getting more confident, the way I'm hitting the ball and seeing what's going on in the match.

"The challenge now is not on the court, it's off the court, to do whatever it takes to be in a good shape and feel physically ready for a battle tomorrow."

Alcaraz is now on a 12-match winning streak and will face Ben Shelton, who he beat in the Paris Masters final last month, in Saturday's semi-finals.

The winner of Friday's last match between Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe will face Alexander Zverev in the other semi-final.

Alcaraz was conservative in his movement, trying to avoid sliding in and out of the corners - but rather than diminishing his game, it allowed him to produce some astonishing shot-making.

Cobolli never looked as though he had the belief that he could challenge Alcaraz, and was broken in the first game of the match by a thumping return winner.

Alcaraz kept the points short, hammering his forehand and backhand to all corners, and targeted Cobolli's second serve in particular.

An astonishing whipped 110mph forehand winner was the highlight of the first set, which Alcaraz wrapped up with a strong service hold.

Cobolli again lost his serve in the opening game of the second set and Alcaraz claimed five of the final six games to secure victory.

After converting match point with another return winner, Alcaraz embraced Cobolli at the net and offered the crushed Italian a few words of support.

Alcaraz has not had his serve broken once in his three group matches as he bids for a first title at the season-ending event.

He and world number one Zverev have both made it through the group stages without dropping a set, while Alcaraz has not lost more than four games in a set.

In the doubles, Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison reached the semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 victory over Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos.

The US Open champions will face fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic for a place in Sunday's final.

title: Disappointing early exit for top seed Julien Carraggi

title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m & delays doubles cuts decision
article_text:
The men's ATP Tour is promising its players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but the board has delayed a decision on hotly disputed changes to doubles until next month.

The bonus pool will increase from the current $21.5m to $50m in 2028, with payments offered to players ranked in the world's top 30 at the start of each Masters 1000 event.

The world number one will receive the highest bonus of $2m for each of the Masters events they play.

A total of $25m will also be shared out between the world's top 250 players at the end of each season, with the goal for everyone to receive $100,000.

That would make a significant difference to the finances of lower-ranked players.

Players will also no longer be penalised so directly for missing tournaments through injury.

World number two Jannik Sinner, for example, won five Masters events in a row between March and May, but may only qualify for 25% of his bonus as he has not been able to play since Wimbledon.

Proposed changes to the doubles - which includes halving draw sizes and reducing the percentage of prize money from 20% to 10% - have received fierce opposition from the players.

In October, more than 150 men's doubles players wrote an open letter to the ATP Tour urging them to reconsider "drastic" changes to the format.

Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi told BBC Sport the governing body of men's tennis needed "a bit more time to reach consensus".

"I hope we find the right balance between the players' and the tournaments' demands, and I truly hope we reach a compromise."

The proposals will now be voted on next month.

Doubles players have said the changes would make it "effectively impossible" for anyone outside the top 30 to make a living from the sport.

There may be a hint of compromise in the air, but Gaudenzi still believes at least some of the doubles money needs to be redirected towards singles players.

"It's impossible to make everyone happy. It's something we do not take lightly, but we also cannot ignore the fans and the broadcasters - [just] like any entertainment business," he said.

"Whether you are a musician or an actor, it needs to be rewarded as a function of the entertainment you provide to the fans."

Gaudenzi told Britain's Henry Patten, who was unhappy he and CEO Eno Polo were not present when Patten and Harri Heliovaara received the year-end number one trophy, that he had no intention of undermining their achievement.

"I understand his disappointment and he's obviously also driven by what we are discussing, and I do understand it's quite emotional their side," Gaudenzi added.

"But I was here in the hotel together with Eno - we were actually fighting and negotiating twelve hours a day to get this deal done - so we were really in the trenches all day long."

The ATP Board has also approved the formation of ATP Ventures, which will bring all the Tour's media, data and central sponsorship rights under the same roof. This could improve the chances of the ATP and the WTA agreeing to pool their resources and create a 'Tennis Ventures'.

Probably the trickiest issue to resolve is the length of the season - there are just 33 days between this year's Davis Cup Finals and the start of the 2027 season in Australia.

The ATP schedule for 2028 is likely to be released in late January, but Gaudenzi warned not to expect "big changes".

"That's going to be difficult," Gaudenzi added.

"The off-season, I think, will improve, but ultimately it will take time.

"But we have a plan, we have shared that plan conceptually with the players and I think it will take a few years to execute, but we are going in the right direction.

"Don't expect big changes regarding the off-season in 2028. They are a work in progress."

title: How sustainability is shaping the Nitto ATP Finals
article_text:
The Nitto ATP Finals is about more than just the on-court action.

As well as bringing together the world's best players for the prestigious year-end tournament, the event provides an opportunity to make a positive impact beyond tennis, with sustainability and community engagement central to its wider ambitions.

At the 2026 edition in Turin, title partner Nitto is continuing its work with the ATP, the Italian Tennis and Padel Federation (FITP) and the City of Turin through the Torino Green Project, while introducing new measures to reduce the tournament's environmental footprint.

For this year's event, a hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) fuel blend is being used in the on-site generators in place of conventional diesel. The generators accounted for 36 per cent of the tournament's emissions in 2025, making this an important step towards the event's goal of reducing carbon emissions by 30 per cent by 2030, compared with 2024 levels. Nitto is supporting that ambition through a five-year commitment.

The initiative builds on the Torino Green Project, launched in 2023 by Nitto, FITP, the City of Turin and the ATP. Its first projects included planting 50 trees near the arena, installing green roofs on selected bus stops and donating €100,000 to the city.

The project has continued to evolve. In 2024, a living Green Wall was installed in the Fan Village and later relocated elsewhere in Turin. In 2025, a Green Art Wall, created using air-purifying Airlite paint, was installed at Leone Sinigaglia primary school.

Other measures supporting the tournament's sustainability efforts include electricity from 100 per cent renewable sources, an electrified Lexus fleet for player and staff transport, discounted Frecciarossa train tickets for fans and free travel on selected tram lines for ticket holders.

Sustainability is also reflected in the tournament's community work. Children and families supported by Turin charity U.G.I. ODV are invited to attend matches, while children have the opportunity to walk on court alongside players as mascots. The Nitto ATP Finals Innovation Summit also brings together representatives from the City of Turin, academia and industry to discuss sustainability challenges.

The tournament's environmental progress is measured by FITP, with support from Enovation Consulting, through carbon-footprint assessments and an annual ESG report. The 2025 edition was also certified to the ISO 20121:2024 sustainable event management standard by Bureau Veritas.

With Nitto's title partnership running through 2030, the host city will continue working with its partners and the to make progress towards its emissions-reduction goal.

title: Zi Yu-Noraqilah reach first Super 500 semi-final in World Tour
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Women's pair Low Zi Yu-Noraqilah Maisarah Ramdan celebrated a major milestone after reaching their first Super 500 semi-final at the Hong Kong Open on Friday.

The world No. 41 upset American world No. 25 Francesca Corbett-Jennie Gai 21-19, 16-21, 21-16 in the quarter-finals at the Kai Tak Arena.

The victory came a day after Zi Yu-Noraqilah upset Taiwan's world No. 6 Hsu Yin Hui-Lin Jhih Yun 21-19, 21-18 in the second round.

"I'm very happy because this is our first Super 500 semi-final," said Zi Yu.

Noraqilah felt the pair had produced their best performance of the week against the Americans.

"I think today we played quite well compared with the two previous matches," she said.

Their creditable run has come despite Noraqilah still working her way back to full fitness following a left ankle injury.

The 19-year-old, who withdrew from last week's Kumamoto Masters, said she was currently at 70 per cent fitness.

Noraqilah said preparation for the Hong Kong Open had been demanding, with Zi Yu returning from junior tournament commitments while she was recovering from injury.

They will face either seniors Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah or another American pair, Lauren Lam-Allison Lee, for a place in the final.

title: Carlos Alcaraz injury update: Spaniard cancels ATP Finals warmup before Flavio Cobolli match

“Well, I feel it a little bit. I’m not gonna lie,” said the 23-year-old.

title: GB's Davis Cup-winning captain ends 17-year stint
article_text:
Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith says it is the "right time" for a change after announcing he will end his 17-year stint in the role.

Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936.

The 50-year-old Scot said he had been mulling over his future for "most of this year" before deciding to step down after next week's Finals in Bologna.

Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible.

Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 triumph, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time.

"There comes a time whether it is personally you need a change, or it is good for the team to have something else," said Smith, who seemed emotional in a video call with reporters.

"I've done it for a very long time and I think there are others who will enjoy the role and can bring something different to the role."

"I love the role and haven't lost any passion for it. But it feels like the right time for me personally and the guys moving forwards."

With Smith picking the team and creating a tight bond between the group, Murray was the driving force on the court as he won all eight of his singles matches in the victorious campaign.

Murray was coached by Smith as a child and said winning the Davis Cup together was "one of the proudest moments" of his career.

"He did a great job of bringing everyone together and making sure we all felt we had a part to play. He got the best out of us that year," three-time Grand Slam champion Murray said.

"I've obviously known Leon a long time, I think the most fun we had together was when I was playing Davis Cup and Leon was on the bench. I'm really glad we got to share those moments.

"I wish Leon all the best as he steps down, and good luck to the new captain."

Smith, who will continue in his role as head of British men's tennis, took over in 2010 with the team in danger of being relegated to the lowest tier of the Davis Cup.

Within three years they were back in the top tier and just two years later Murray inspired them to the trophy.

Smith also guided the team to the semi-finals in 2016 and 2019.

While he can no longer rely on a superstar of Murray's ilk, Smith is hoping this year's crop can ensure his captaincy ends on another high.

Britain will rely on Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery and former world number eight Cameron Norrie in the singles, with world number one Henry Patten and three-time major champion Neal Skupski pairing up in the doubles.

Smith's side faces Germany - led by singles world number one Alexander Zverev - in the last eight on Thursday.

"I'm focused and really looking forward to captaining Great Britain for one more week in Bologna next week and hopefully creating a few more special memories together," Smith added.

Smith has won 70% of his ties since taking over as captain in the summer of 2010.

The venues and the crowds for many of the early ties were on the low side, until Britain moved through the divisions and Andy Murray returned to the team.

The travelling support surged, and the team celebrated their return to the World Group with a stunning win over the United States in a baseball stadium in San Diego in January 2014.

Less than two years later the Davis Cup was back in Britain as thrilling wins in Glasgow and the Queen's Club were followed by Murray's famous lob to seal victory over Belgium.

Great attention to detail has contributed to Britain's success; and far more often than not, Smith got the marginal selection calls right.

He will be an extremely hard act to follow, but will inevitably work closely with his successor given his ongoing role as the head of men's tennis.

title: Leon Smith: Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain stepping down after 17 years
article_text:
Great Britain's Davis Cup-winning captain Leon Smith says it is the "right time" for a change after announcing he will end his 17-year stint in the role.

Smith guided the British men's team to Davis Cup victory in 2015 - the nation's first win in the event since 1936.

The 50-year-old Scot said he had been mulling over his future for "most of this year" before deciding to step down after next week's Finals in Bologna.

Smith's successor has not yet been appointed, but the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) has spoken to potential candidates and hopes to announce the new captain as soon as possible.

Former world number one Andy Murray, who was instrumental in Britain's 2015 triumph, is not believed to be interested in the role at this time.

title: Hong Kong Open: Evergreen Intanon Books Record Trip
article_text:
Ratchanok Intanon punched her ticket to the season finale for a women’s singles record 11th time after beating Michelle Li 21-19 21-16 in the LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 quarterfinals on Friday.

Needing a victory to secure the ranking points required for next month’s HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 in Hangzhou, the Thai star showed trademark composure to reach her first Hong Kong Open semifinal since finishing runner-up to Chen Yu Fei in 2019.

“I felt like she had some pain or some injury,” Intanon said of Li. “Still, I tried not to think about anything outside the court and just focus on the game. I had to stay calm on every shot because I felt she was slower than me, though her hands were still better than mine on some shots.”

For Intanon, the milestone is a testament to resilience following her own injury battles.

“First of all, I want to thank myself because I never give up through injuries,” she reflected. “Coming back takes time and I’ve tried to take it slowly and manage it with my coach. Even here, I’m still not 100 per cent, so I just wanted to do what I could in the moment.”

Next up is an all-Thai semifinal against compatriot Pornpawee Chochuwong, who defeated Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj by the exact same scoreline moments later. Chochuwong also clinched the final women’s singles berth for Hangzhou after her sole rival, Putri Kusuma Wardani, fell 22-20 22-20 to Wang Zhi Yi.

Despite making 10 prior appearances at the season finale, a title has remained elusive for Intanon.

Her first appearance back in 2012 – at the Super Series Finals – saw her reach the last four, where she lost to Wang Shi Xian.

“I’ve played so many times now. I’m always very grateful and though I’ve never won it, every time I go I hope to at least make that semifinal mark,” she said. “I’m going to take care of my body after this tournament and try to get stronger.”

Asked if she is setting a bigger target this year, her answer was simple: “Winning.”

Amallia Cahaya Pratiwi/Siti Fadia Silva Ramadhanti completed their remarkable rise by claiming a women’spot at the Finals, beating top seeds Yuki Fukushima/Mayu Matsumoto 21-16 21-15.

Languishing in 23rd position just last month, the Indonesians, who only paired up this year, surged into the women’s doubles top eight off the back of a HYLO Open title, deep runs at the French Open and Kumamoto Masters and Friday’s upset. Minutes later, Americans Lauren Lam/Allison Lee’s 21-18 21-11 defeat to Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan officially sealed Hangzhou berths for both Pratiwi/Ramadhanti and Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva/Stefani Stoeva.

Pratiwi put their qualification into perspective: “Opportunities truly come from anywhere; we didn’t expect to make it this far.”

Ramadhanti added: “Going through a difficult period and missing out on the Asian Games really served as a wake-up call for us.”

title: Arthur Fils & Rafael Jodar’s ATP Finals ranking points & prize money after round robin exits
article_text:
Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar have both been eliminated from the 2026 ATP Finals, but how many ranking points and how much prize money did they earn?

Jodar had to beat Ben Shelton on Thursday to keep his hopes of progressing to the semi-finals alive, but his 7-6(8), 7-5 defeat to the American meant he finished bottom of the John McEnroe Group.

The Spanish star’s loss to Shelton saw him finish with a 0-3 record after he was beaten by Alexander Zverev and Arthur Fils in his first two matches.

After Shelton’s victory over Jodar, Fils required a straight-set win over Zverev in the final match in the John McEnroe Group on Thursday evening to qualify for the last four.

However, Fils was eliminated as he suffered a 6-4, 7-6(4) defeat to the world No 1.

The Frenchman lost to Shelton in his opening match before defeating Jodar in his second.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Both Jodar and Fils were making their debuts at the ATP Finals.

Zverev won the John McEnroe Group with a 3-0 record, while Shelton finished in second place after winning two of his three matches.

Fils collected 200 ATP ranking points for his round robin win against Jodar. He has overtaken Flavio Cobolli to climb to a projected new career-high position of world No 6 in the ATP Live Rankings.

Jodar, meanwhile, did not add to his points tally after losing all three of his matches in Turin. He remains 10th in the rankings.

Both Fils and Jodar earned a participation fee of $338,000 for playing all of their round robin matches.

Fils earned an additional $405,000 for his victory.

title: BWF World Senior Circuit Hosting Opportunity – 2027
article_text:
Building on the initial circuit tournaments in 2026, and after consultation with key stakeholders, the BWF has confirmed a framework for the BWF World Senior Circuit and welcomes applications from interested Member Associations to host tournaments in 2027.

The establishment of the World Senior Circuit is a key strategic opportunity to engage senior players on a global level to continue to play badminton and to invest in a circuit of sustainable tournaments which culminate in the BWF World Senior Championships as the pinnacle senior badminton tournament.

The following summarises the established framework and application process.

- As a standalone World Senior Circuit tournament or as a joint Continental Confederation Senior Circuit and BWF Senior Circuit tournament.

- The BWF to sanction/confirm World Senior Circuit tournaments.

- Host responsible for delivery of tournament and related costs.

Same as World Senior Championships starting with 35+ up to 75+ with host option to hold more categories (e.g. 80+).

Additional strength categories can be offered (e.g. recreational or a “waterfall” tournament); however, the elite category only counts for the World Senior Ranking.

Player Age Eligibility: Players must fulfil the age requirement before 1 January of the year of the tournament.

- Manual entry process to start (or tournament-specific online entry if applicable).

- Entry fees can be charged to ensure operational sustainability.

- Maximum three events per player (per age group or across varying age groups).

- Group > Knockout if entry size requires (group only if entry size requires) following, where applicable, BWF General Competition Regulations (GCR).

Scoring System: Best of three games to 15 points.

Length of competition up to host based on entry size and other local factors, with last day (finals) on Sunday.

- Prospectus Publication: At least 120 days in advance of tournament.

- Entry deadline: Four weeks in advance of tournament.

- Draws: One week in advance of tournament.

- Based on World Senior Ranking, where applicable, following GCR.

- Substitutions: Allowed for doubles events only, as per BWF World Senior Championships regulations.

- Minimum national level but Continental Level recommended.

- Minimum national level but Continental Level recommended.

- Line Judges: Recruited and provided by host.

Transportation Services: Determined by host, based on entry fees charged.

Accommodation: Determined by host, but at minimum, host to provide list of hotel options for individual player bookings.

Visa Support: Hosting MA to provide visa support letter / other documentation as required.

- Tournament doctor / nurse / paramedics for field of play.

- Medical care for players provided back of house as needed but can be charged to players.

Practice: Where feasible, provide access to competition courts (and practice court(s), if available), but not required.

A set of formalised regulations will be confirmed and published based on the above framework in due course.

The BWF is accepting applications from Member Associations to host World Senior Circuit tournaments in 2027 (with the option to confirm continued hosting in 2028) through submission of a Sanction Request by 31 December 2026 via the following form.

Please note that for 2027 tournaments, the earliest hosting opportunity would be March 2027.

The BWF to confirm hosts by January 2027 and establish a calendar of tournaments.

The BWF to provide further guidance to hosting Member Associations in January or February 2027.

title: Miyazaki avenges Akechi and faces Wang in Hong Kong Open semifinals
article_text:
Tomoka Miyazaki, Japan's next-generation women's badminton star and the world No. 7, swept past compatriot Hina Akechi, ranked No. 14, to avenge her loss at the Korea Open and reach the Hong Kong Open semifinals.

Miyazaki beat Akechi 2-0 (21-11, 21-9) in the women's singles quarterfinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Hong Kong Open (Super 500) on the 20th at Kai Tak Arena in Hong Kong.

It was a dominant victory. Miyazaki trailed 4-2 early in the first game but reeled off five straight points to take a 7-4 lead. She extended it to 10-5, and when Akechi began to close the gap, Miyazaki scored five consecutive points again to go ahead 15-6. She eventually took the first game 21-11.

The second game followed a similar pattern. Leading 2-1 early on, Miyazaki won seven points in a row to go up 9-1. Akechi fought back to 13-8, but Miyazaki won five straight points to seal the momentum. She closed out the match 21-9.

The victory means more than simply reaching the semifinals. On the 6th, Miyazaki lost to Akechi in the Korea Open women's singles quarterfinals in Yeosu, South Jeolla province, falling 2-1 (13-21, 23-21, 21-8) after taking the first game.

The Hong Kong Open is a good opportunity for Miyazaki to contend for the title. The top three in the women's singles rankings — world No. 1 Ahn Se-young, No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi of Japan and No. 5 Pusarla Venkata Sindhu of India — are all absent.

Miyazaki has already secured a spot in the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals. If she wins her first title of the season at this tournament, she can build her confidence ahead of the season-ending finals next month.

Miyazaki will face Wang Zhiyi in the semifinals. Wang beat Indonesia's Putri Kusuma Wardani 2-0 (22-20, 22-20) in an earlier quarterfinal.

After avenging her Korea Open loss to Akechi, Miyazaki now has a chance to get back at Wang Zhiyi, who eliminated her at the Kumamoto Masters. She is just two wins away from her first title of the season.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026: Lakshya Sen overcomes Loh Kean Yew in three games to enter semis
article_text:
Lakshya Sen beat Singapore’s Loh Kean Yew 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 to advance to the semifinals at the Hong Kong Open on Friday.

Lakshya made a brisk start to take an 11-7 lead into the interval, but Loh fought back strongly to draw level at 14-14. The two traded points in a tense finish before Lakshya found another gear to take the opening game 21-17.

Loh seized control early in the second game, racing to a 7-2 lead and carrying a comfortable 11-6 advantage into the interval. He continued to dominate after the break, stretching the lead to 19-10 before closing out the game 21-10 to force a decider.

Lakshya bounced back emphatically in the decider, racing to an 11-5 lead at the interval. He maintained his grip on the contest after the break, stretching the advantage to 19-10 before sealing the game 21-13 to complete a hard-fought victory.

Earlier, Lakshya, who is now assured of a spot at BWF Tour Finals 2026, beat Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in straight games in the round of 16.

Lakshya revived his season in emphatic fashion, winning back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and Japan Masters to emerge as a strong contender for the BWF World Tour Finals. His triumph in Japan, where he defeated Koki Watanabe in the final, proved crucial to his qualification bid, as he closed in on becoming only the second Indian after P. V. Sindhu (women’s singles) to make the cut for this year’s season-ending tournament.

Lakshya last featured in the BWF World Tour Finals in 2021, reaching the semifinals.

title: De Minaur to headline major Australian tournament amid form slump
article_text:
Alex de Minaur will take part in the Brisbane International for the first time in eight years, announcing he will play the Australian Open lead-up tournament in January.

In doing so, he becomes the biggest marquee player to sign up for the event since Rafael Nadal, Novak Djokovic and Andy Murray did so across the early 2020s.

It is also the event where Nick Kyrgios made his fleeting attempt at a singles return in 2026, before opting out of an Australian Open wildcard spot.

The tournament gets underway in the first week of January and de Minaur is excited to build into what will be a crucial calendar year for him.

“I love playing on Pat Rafter Arena and have so many fond memories of competing in Brisbane. The support is always awesome, and I can’t wait to get back out there,” de Minaur said.

“There’s nothing better than playing at home in Australia. The first week of the year is a great opportunity to get the season off to a strong start, and Brisbane is the perfect place to do that.

“It’ll be a strong field, as always, but you can’t beat winning at home, so I’ll be doing everything I can to lift the trophy in Brisbane.”

It marks the starting point of what the 27-year-old hopes will be a form turning point, after a difficult 2026 season.

De Minaur will enter 2027 as the No.11 ranked player in the world, after being as high as fifth in July.

A second round exit at the US Open coupled with poor performances on the ATP Tour in the second half of the year ultimately cost him from a ranking perspective.

The Aussie admits he has to change his mindset going forward and learn from what has turned into a form slump.

“It’s the first time that I’ve felt the inconsistency,” de Minaur told the Associated Press.

“I went through a six-month period where I kind of went walkabout. I wasn’t myself. I wasn’t playing the type of tennis that I know I could and I missed out on a lot of opportunities.

“I’ve been spoiled in a way that I’ve been able to bring that level week in and week out and for the longest time I almost expected those wins.

“I’ve got to be a little bit nicer to myself and appreciative of winning any sort of match.

“I was still worried about the level I was playing and I wasn’t content with myself.

“That carried on to the whole clay season and then it became a little bit of a snowball effect.”

Performance on the big stage in Grand Slams has also come into focus for de Minaur.

Despite sitting in-and-around the top 10 since 2023, he has had a tendency to stumble when it matters most.

De Minaur is yet to advance beyond a Grand Slam quarter-final at any of the four majors to this point of his career.

He made the quarter-final in the 2026 Australian Open before losing to Carlos Alcaraz, and stumbled in early phases of the other three Slams, missing out on golden opportunities to advance deep while Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner missed time with injuries.

“That’s one of the key things I want to focus on and try to go deep at the Slams,” he said.

“Really try to prioritise that a little bit more to make sure that all my energy goes towards those events.”

He has made the last two Australian Open quarter-finals, and will be hoping 2027 is the year he pushes deeper on his home turf.

title: Alexander Zverev suffers injury scare as Carlos Alcaraz discovers his fate at ATP Finals
article_text:
Alexander Zverev cleared some of the fog around the group phase of the ATP Finals as he powered to a third successive straight sets win by seeing off the challenge of Arthur Fils in Turin.

Zverev highlighted his impressive record against top ten rivals who are not Jannik Sinner or Carlos Alcaraz in a press conference earlier this week and he has backed up those words by adding another three wins to his record this week.

Zverev has seen off Rafael Jodar, Ben Shelton and now Fils in convincing fashion, with his latest win ensuring Shelton will progress to a potential semi-final clash against Alcaraz on Saturday.

There are doubts over whether Alcaraz will compete in the latter stages of the ATP Finals after he injured his hamstring in his win against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday, but he now knows another match against Shelton awaits if he is fit enough to compete.

Alcaraz went for a scan on his hamstring on Thursday morning and it has been decided that he will try to compete in the rest of the tournament, but that position could change if his condition worsens.

Zverev also suffered an injury scare in his win against Fils, as he admitted a long-standing ankle problem was giving him some concern.

The pain he feels is linked to the huge injury he suffered in his 2022 French Open semi-final against Rafael Nadal, as he conceded it still gives him pain.

“Unfortunately I started feeling my ankle again,” Zverev said after his 6-4, 7-6(6) victory.

“I’ll probably feel my ankle sometimes until the end of my career. Unfortunately, the injury that I had was quite big. I’m going to do everything that I can to be pain-free on Saturday, but this is something I have to live with nowadays.”

Zverev also admitted some of his intensity was lacking against Fils as he knew his place in the semi-finals was already secured.

“I thought the first two matches were very high level,” he added.

“Today I thought I played a little bit worse from the baseline, but I’m very happy to have won all three matches, against three very difficult opponents.

“Arthur, for me personally, is a very difficult opponent because of how much power he has, but I’m happy to be through in straight sets.”

Zverev is set to play Daniil Medvedev in the last four on Saturday, with Alcaraz taking on Shelton if he can manage his hamstring problem.

title: ATP Finals 2026 Day 5 Recap
article_text:
Day 5 of the 2026 ATP Finals saw Alexander Zverev complete a perfect round-robin campaign, while Ben Shelton booked his place in the semi-finals after a hard-fought victory over Rafael Jodar.

Shelton survived two set points in a tight opening-set tiebreak before eventually seeing off the Spaniard in straight sets, although he had to wait for the evening result to confirm his qualification.

Zverev then defeated Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6), despite the Frenchman saving five consecutive match points in a dramatic second-set tiebreak. The German tops the John McEnroe Group with three wins from three and hasn’t dropped a service game all week.

The result sets up a semi-final between Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz, while Zverev will face the winner of Friday’s clash between Daniil Medvedev and Frances Tiafoe.

Both Zverev and Alcaraz look a level above the rest so far, although a few physical concerns remain heading into the knockout stages, with Alcaraz nursing a hamstring issue and Zverev also appearing uncomfortable towards the end of his match.

Ben Shelton (3) def. Rafael Jodar (8) 7-6(8), 7-5

Ben Shelton kept his ATP Finals semi-final hopes alive on Thursday afternoon, defeating Rafael Jodar 7-6(8), 7-5 in a hard-fought encounter.

The American, who lost to Alexander Zverev on Tuesday, had to work considerably harder than expected against the 20-year-old Spaniard, eventually coming through in two hours and seven minutes.

The opening set was closely contested, with Jodar putting Shelton under pressure on serve and creating break opportunities. However, the American escaped trouble with his usual big serving, and the pair eventually headed to a tiebreak.

Jodar had two set points in the breaker, but Shelton saved both before finally taking it 10-8 when the Spaniard framed a forehand long.

The second set was another tight affair, though Shelton looked to have taken control after moving up to 4-2. However, Jodar refused to go away, fighting back to level at 5-5 with aggressive baseline hitting.

At that point, it looked like we might be heading for another tiebreak, but Shelton produced one of his better return games to break at 5-5, moving Jodar from corner to corner before serving out the match.

It wasn’t really a convincing display from Shelton from the baseline, and he basically relied heavily on his serve to get himself out of trouble.

Jodar had plenty of opportunities and probably should have taken the opening set, but he looked a bit leggy, especially when moving forward to track down Shelton’s shorter slices.

Jodar finishes his ATP Finals debut with three defeats, but his rise from No. 168 at the start of the year to the world’s top ten is one of the season’s stories, and he’s certainly one to watch next year.

Shelton, meanwhile, finishes the round-robin stage at 2-1 and must now wait for the result of Alexander Zverev’s match against Arthur Fils.

If Fils wins in straight sets, the Frenchman will progress alongside Zverev. Any other result will see Shelton qualify for the semi-finals in second place.

Alexander Zverev (1) def. Arthur Fils 6-4 7-6(6)

Alexander Zverev completed a perfect round-robin campaign at the 2026 ATP Finals on Thursday evening, defeating Arthur Fils 6-4, 7-6(6) to finish top of the John McEnroe Group without dropping a set.

The World No. 1, who had already secured his semi-final spot with victories over Rafael Jodar and Ben Shelton, made a solid start against the Frenchman, relying on his excellent serving and consistent baseline game.

Fils played some decent tennis in the opening set, but a sloppy service game at 3-3 proved costly. Zverev converted his third break point to move 4-3 ahead and comfortably served out the set 6-4 in around 35 minutes, ending Fils’ hopes of reaching the semi-finals and confirming Shelton’s qualification.

However, I liked how Fils tried to play, and he wasn’t about to roll over as the second set proved far more competitive.

The Frenchman raised his level, going toe-to-toe with Zverev from the baseline (who I thought didn’t hit his forehand as well), and showing the aggressive tennis that has propelled him into the Top 8 despite posting a woeful Grand Slam record.

Neither player could find the breakthrough until Fils earned two set points on Zverev’s serve at 6-5. However, Sascha produced some huge serves to escape trouble and force a tiebreak.

Zverev then won six consecutive points to lead 6-1, seemingly putting the match to bed, but Fils remarkably saved five straight match points to level at 6-6.

However, Sascha eventually got the job done, taking the breaker 8-6 to seal another straight-sets victory.

Fils put in a decent effort, and if he’d been a little wiser on some points, he’d have taken a set, but he ultimately couldn’t get past Zverev when it mattered.

For the German, it’s been an excellent group stage. Three matches, three victories, and six sets won without dropping a single one. He’s also gone through all three matches without losing a service game, which is pretty impressive given the opposition, but not so surprising given he’s bombing down 185 km/h second serves, on average.

Zverev advances to the semi-finals as the John McEnroe Group winner and will face either Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe, who meet on Friday to decide the second qualifying spot from the Ivan Lendl Group.

Shelton also advances despite his Tuesday defeat to Zverev and will face Carlos Alcaraz in the other semi-final.

title: A 15-year ATP Tour streak has just been broken by Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, and Alexander Zverev
article_text:
Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, and Jannik Sinner have comfortably been the best three players on the ATP Tour this year.

Zverev has managed to claim the first two Grand Slam titles of his career, which subsequently helped him become world No 1 for the first time too.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, began the year with an Australian Open victory, before ending the year on a high with wins in Vienna and Paris after a four and a half month injury absence.

Sinner, too, has suffered with injuries, but he was still able to win the first five Masters titles of the season, as well as his fifth Grand Slam at Wimbledon.

The pair are far and away the top three ranked players on the ATP Tour, as they have been for the past three seasons.

Zverev, Alcaraz, and Sinner have become the first trio of players in 11 years to keep their place in the top three of the rankings for three consecutive seasons.

The last trio to do so was, unsurprisingly, Novak Djokovic, Roger Federer, and Rafael Nadal, who stayed top three for five years in a row between 2007 and 2011.

Zverev, Alcaraz, and Sinner have become just the third trio in men’s tennis history to earn the accolade, also joining Jimmy Connors, Ivan Lendl, and John McEnroe.

Those three tennis legends stayed in the top three between the 1981 and 1984 season, so the current best three players in the world are in very good company.

There is little reason to believe that they will not continue that form into the 2027 season either, particularly with how this season has gone.

Sinner has missed six months of action and Alcaraz has missed four and a half months and yet neither came anywhere near close to losing their position in the top three of the ATP Tour rankings.

As things stand, Alcaraz, who is the current world No 3, sits 1200 ranking points above Ben Shelton in the rankings, and that looks destined to increase at the ATP Finals.

A potential hamstring injury aside, Alcaraz is one of the major favourites to win the ATP Finals and it would be a big surprise to not see him make the final.

The Spaniard could create yet more distance between world No 3 and world No 4 as the 2026 season draws to a close.

It’s hard to see anyone having the consistency to dislodge Zverev, Sinner, and Alcaraz from the rankings, despite the likes of Shelton, Arthur Fils, and Flavio Cobolli making giant strides in the rankings this season.

title: Alcaraz Cleared to Continue ATP Finals, But Risk Remains
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has reportedly received encouraging news regarding his left hamstring injury and has decided to continue competing at the ATP Finals in Turin.

According to reports from Spanish media, including Punto de Break, Cadena COPE and RTVE, an MRI conducted on Thursday ruled out structural damage to the Spaniard’s left hamstring, clearing the way for him to face Flavio Cobolli on Friday.

Note: Alcaraz has already qualified for the semifinals, so the stakes of Friday’s match aren’t as high as they might have been had he been preparing to play for qualifying for the semifinals.

It doesn’t necessarily mean the 23-year-old, who cancelled today’s practice with junior No.1 Guto Miguel of Brazil, is out of the woods.

Cadena SER reports that Alcaraz’s team is taking a cautious, match-by-match approach, with the seven-time Grand Slam champion expected to evaluate his physical condition following Friday’s encounter before making any decisions about the semifinals.

Friday’s match with Cobolli should give him the information he needs to decide whether or not he feels good enough to make a run at winning the title in Turin.

There is also the matter of Alcaraz’s right knee, which had been troubling him ahead of the tournament. RTVE reported that Thursday’s medical examinations also addressed the knee, but no specific findings have been made public.

It all adds up to a delicate situation for Alcaraz, who has plenty at stake beyond this week’s competition in Turin. The Spaniard is expected to represent his country at the Davis Cup Finals later this month, and the pressure to compete for his nation will undoubtedly weigh heavily on him.

There is also the bigger picture to consider.

With the 2027 season fast approaching, Alcaraz will have a relatively short offseason to recover, rebuild and prepare for his Australian Open title defense.

But the combination of hamstring discomfort and an ongoing knee concern makes this an especially important moment for the Spaniard. Tempted by winning the ATP Finals and then representing Spain at Davis Cup could come at a cost. He’ll have to listen closely to his body, and make a decision that balances the present and the future.

title: 'I was scared': LPGA player confesses to lying about rules breach before DQ
article_text:
For Scarlett Schremmer, the 2026 ANNIKA event was supposed to be the start of a promising LPGA career. Instead, the University of Miami golfer was left “embarrassed” following a rules breach that resulted in her disqualification.

As if a college golfer getting DQ’d in her LPGA debut wasn’t bad enough, the story took a turn for the worse this week.

On Friday, Schremmer took to Instagram to deliver a surprising confession: she lied to LPGA rules officials when questioned about the rules breach that led to her DQ.

On Saturday at last week’s ANNIKA event, the LPGA announced that Schremmer had been disqualified for a rules breach. Schremmer’s offense was using a yardage book prohibited by a Model Local Rule in place at all LPGA Tour events.

Following her DQ, Schremmer broke her silence in a statement on Instagram, saying she “had a green reading yardage book in my bag this week that’s allowed in college golf but isn’t permitted on the LPGA Tour. That’s on me. I should have checked, and it’s a lesson learned.”

What she didn’t admit to was using the illegal yardage book during the tournament. But Golfweek’s Beth Ann Nichols later reported that LPGA rules officials had been alerted to Schremmer’s use of the illegal yardage book as early as Thursday’s first round. Those officials took no action until photo evidence of Schremmer’s offenses turned up on Saturday.

Nichols’ report also included one more detail that contradicted Schremmer’s initial statement. When questioned about the yardage book, Schremmer denied using it.

That changed on Friday, when Schremmer released a new statement on Instagram. This time, the college golfer admitted to wrongly telling rules officials that the illegal yardage book in her bag was “not in use.” Schremmer also apologized for her “extremely poor decision,” saying fear and embarrassment led her to lie.

“When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use,” Schremmer wrote on Instagram on Friday. “I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.”

She continued by writing that golf had taught her about “integrity, accountability, and respect for the game,” and that her actions during the ANNIKA event “did not reflect those values or the person I strive to be.”

Schremmer also said that she hopes to rebuild her reputation “through actions rather than words” over time.

You can read Schremmer’s full Instagram statement below.

“Over the past few days, I’ve spent a lot of time reflecting on what happened last week and, more importantly, how I handled the situation. I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use. I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.

“Golf has taught me so much about integrity, accountability, and respect for the game. More than anything, I genuinely love playing golf, and I have always understood that being a competitor means respecting the game and the standards that come with it. I know that my actions and the way I handled this situation did not reflect those values or the person I strive to be. This experience has given me a lot to think about, both as a golfer and as a person. I understand that trust is earned through actions rather than words, and I know that rebuilding it takes time. I am committed to learning from this, growing through it, and demonstrating through my actions that I can move forward with greater honesty, maturity and accountability.”

title: LPGA Commish on Tour’s New Vision
LPGA all-time money list: Three active players closing in on Annika Sorenstam’s record
article_text:
Annika Sorenstam’s grip on the LPGA Tour’s all-time money list is nearing an end.

Sorenstam’s 25-year record of $22,583,693 could finally be trumped on Sunday at the CME Group Tour Championship.

Nelly Korda, Lydia Ko and Jeeno Thitikul are all primed to take Sorenstam’s No. 1 spot. How long will that player hold on to the title is the real question.

Korda is second on the list, $160,000 shy of Sorenstam. And after her is Ko, followed by Karrie Webb and Thitikul.

Thitikul’s most recent win in Hawaii moved her over Cristie Kerr for fifth place, and she entered the season-finale just a few dollars off Webb’s fourth-place mark. Let’s take a look at the current top 20 all-time (as of Nov. 21):

- Ko: Needs a solo fifth-place finish or better.

Entering the final round, Korda is T-4, two shots back of A Lim Kim’s lead. Thitikul is T-2, one shot off the lead at 17 under.

Ko won’t challenge for the top money spot this week. She sits in last place at 11 over after opening her tournament 77-78-72.

The season-ending championship features a $4 million prize for the winner and $1 million for the runner-up, prizes that are justifiably capable of shaking up the top of the list.

title: DQ'd college golfer admits lying to officials during LPGA rules inquiry
article_text:
It was a tough look for Scarlett Schremmer. The University of Miami sophomore golfer was gifted a coveted sponsor’s exemption as an amateur into last week’s The Annika tournament on the LPGA Tour that is hosted by Hall of Famer Annika Sorenstam. Schremmer got the opportunity because her Hurricanes teammate, social media darling Kai Trump, couldn’t participate in the event for a second straight year after undergoing wrist surgery.

Schremmer’s qualifcations to receive a chance were arguably stronger than Trump’s, with the Alabama native having won two college tournaments in the fall while being a member of the prestigious USGA’s 2026 Elite Amateur Program.

But a week full of opportunity turned into a nightmare when, after Schremmer missed the cut, the LPGA announced on Saturday that she had been disqualified for violating Model Local Rule G-11 by using a yardage book that was not approved by the tour.

Schremmer then spun a further web of confusion. One of her professional playing partners for the first two days, Perrine Delacour, called out LPGA officials on X with: "Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies.” Delacour confirmed to Golfweek that she had spoken to rules officials about Schremmer's use of the book.

Schremmer, whose mother, former LPGA player Patricia Ehrhart, was her caddie for the week, reportedly denied to rules officials that she had used an illegal book, and in a statement that Saturday she provided a to Golfweek, Schremmer said, "I had a green reading yardage book in my bag this week that’s allowed in college golf but isn’t permitted on the LPGA Tour. That’s on me. I should have checked, and it’s a lesson learned." The statement was somewhat confusing and left open the possiblity that Schremmer was contending that the book was in her bag but she didn't use it.

That was Schremmer’s lone public comment on the matter until she wrote another post on Instragram on Friday, Nov. 20, and admitted that she lied to officials by saying she had not used the yardage book in question.

"Over the past few days, I've spent a lot of time reflecting on what happened last week and, more importantly, how I handled the situation,” Schremmer wrote. “I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use. I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.

"Golf has taught me so much about integrity, accountability, and respect for the game. More than anything, I genuinely love playing golf, and I have always understood that being a competitor means respecting the game and the standards that come with it. I know that my actions and the way I handled this situation did not reflect those values or the person I strive to be. This experience has given me a lot to think about, both as a golfer and as a person. I understand that trust is earned through actions rather than words, and I know that rebuilding it takes time. I am committed to learning from this, growing through it, and demonstrating through my actions that I can move forward with greater honesty, maturity and accountability."

It remains to be seen how the incident follows Schremmer into the future. It’s not the first time a young player has made a sizeable mistake by not telling the truth.

Korean professional Ina Yoon is still dealing with seeing headlines and references to stories for her cheating scandal in 2022.

Yoon was a 19-year-old pro rookie when she knowingly played the wrong ball in the South Korean Open and chose not report it. It would take another month for Yoon to admit her mistake, and the Korean Golf Association and KLPGA issued a three-year suspension that was eventually reduced to 18 months.

The incident didn't ruin Yoon's career. She later donated the money she earned on mini-tours during the ban to junior golf, and in 2025 she earned her way onto the LPGA, where she has become a formidable competitor. Yoon has four top-five finishes this season, finshed solo second in the major KMPG Women’s PGA Championship, and now ranks 17th in the world.

title: Kim holds one-shot lead at LPGA finale as Korda closes in
article_text:
South Korea's A-Lim Kim holds a slender lead going into the final round of the CME Group Tour Championship, with world number one Nelly Korda among the chasers.

Kim, who held a three-shot overnight lead, carded a third round 69 which included six birdies and three bogeys, with two of those coming on the final three holes, to reach 18 under overall.

"I really focused on my game. Just aim and hit, that's all," said Kim.

"Today the wind direction [was a] little tricky, changed a lot, swirly in the air. That's golf."

In the chase for the $4m (£3.1m) top prize at the season-ending event, Japan's Yuri Yoshida and Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand are both on 17 under - one shot behind Kim.

Korda was six shots off the lead before round three, but produced a superb 65 to move to 16 under.

The American, who will qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame if she wins on Sunday, fired nine birdies in a seven-under-par round which also included two bogeys.

England's Charley Hull is on 14 under following a 69 as she carded four birdies and a bogey on Saturday around the Tiburon Golf Club in Florida.
